News.title: American Airlines flights grounded nationwide as company hit by ‘systemwide IT outage’
News.content:
FLIGHT CHAOS American Airlines flights grounded nationwide as company hit by ‘systemwide IT outage’

AMERICAN Airlines grounded all of its flights nationwide after the company was hit by a “systemwide IT outage”, the FAA said.

The carrier was unable to let aircraft on the ground take off and planes had to sit at their gates waiting for the all clear.



The stoppage took effect from 6.30pm ET on Tuesday and applied to all flights and facilities run by the airline.

On social media the airline said: “Our IT team is working as quickly as possible to get our system back up.”



They later continued: “We put a temporary ground stop in place while our teams worked to resolve the issue. We apologize to our customers for the inconvenience.”

At about 7.20pm the airline said “systems are coming back online now and flights are departing again.”



Flightradar24 said American and regional carriers operating on its behalf had 130 fewer flights airborne than the same time last week.

News.title: Moment asylum seeker, 21, is arrested with 7-inch knife and petrol can outside school in bid to ‘set building on fire’
News.content:
THIS is the moment a failed asylum seeker was arrested in possession of a 7-inch knife and petrol can outside a school.

South Sudanese national Both Douk Deng, 21, was arrested after workmen confronted him on the premises of Edgar Wood Academy in Heywood, Greater Manchester, on August 6 last year.



A member of the public earlier raised the alarm after he was observed “behaving oddly” in the street nearby en route to the secondary school holding a petrol can with a hammer tied to his belt.

Deng was “mumbling” as he walked a “full circuit” around the school, which was closed to pupils for the summer, as he scanned the building and then approached it before builders working on site became concerned and called the police.



CCTV footage released by Greater Manchester Police showed Deng kicking over a traffic cone as he walked into the school’s premises and then stamping on another road sign aggressively.

He can also be seen appearing to wave, while carrying the green petrol can, at the workmen who approached him inside the school.



A police car then pulled up near the school and bodycam footage showed Deng wailing as he was wrestled to the ground by a police officer.

Deng is told to “stop there” by the officer, who then tells him to “get on the ground now” as he attempts to run away.



An officer can then be heard saying: “He does have a hammer with him as well. And a hatchet.”

Footage then shows Deng being led away in handcuffs to a police van.

Along with the hammer and hatchet, he was found to be in possession of a seven-inch kitchen knife, and a jerry can containing half a litre of petrol.

A day earlier he was spotted “acting oddly” at another school, Holy Family RC and CE College in Rochdale, also closed to pupils, where he kicked and damaged its intercom.

Deng, who has applied for and been refused asylum on three occasions, wanted to “create a scene for attention” to aid his cause, Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court heard.



Sara Haque, defending, said: “He maintains that his actions were not motivated by any desire to injury or harm any person.

“This was a bizarre and compulsive act lacking in any type of maturity at a time when he was in deep distress having left Sudan and his family in traumatic circumstances.

“He wanted attention and he was in crisis but he was not motivated by hostility towards children, teachers or the wider public.

“There is no evidence that he threatened any individual.”

Deng, who has a wife and children, was placed in multiple accommodation housing (HMO) on his arrival in the UK, the court was told.



Ms Haque said: “He found himself in a foreign country with very limited English and unable to work because of his immigration status.

“He believed and felt no-one was listening to him and no-one was helping him.

“He felt he had reached the of his ability to cope within the HMO where others in similar circumstances to him had been assisted by the immigration authorities.

“He became increasingly frustrated that the same was not happening for him.

“His only wish is to work and find money to support his family.”



Psychiatric reports on the defendant had not identified any major mental health issues, the court heard.

Deng, of Heywood, pleaded guilty at an earlier hearing to a range of offences including criminal damage and possessing weapons and a knife in a public place and on school premises.

Deng was told he must serve up to half his sentence in custody and the remainder on licence.

Judge Bernadette Baxter told him: “I have no power to order the Home Office to do anything.

“But in my judgment, given your circumstances as a failed asylum seeker who has been in custody for the best part of a year, the Home Office should be doing something rather than nothing to deal with your status in this country.”



Detectives from Rochdale CID worked “thoroughly” to investigate Deng, including examining his mobile phone, but found no evidence of a particular motive or intent, said police.

Chief superintendent Helen Caldbeck, district commander for Rochdale, said: “I’m incredibly proud of the officers’ response to this incident.

“They were professional and brave in tackling a suspicious man armed with weapons and immediately confronted Deng to keep the public safe.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Thankfully no one was close to coming to harm but this was nevertheless a disturbing incident.”

Deng was sentenced to two years in prison.

News.title: Andy Burnham vows to put ‘everything I’ve got’ into fixing England’s crumbling adult social care system
News.content:
ANDY Burnham pledged to put “everything I’ve got” at fixing England’s crumbling adult social care system.

The Prime Minister handed out an olive branch to Kemi Badenoch and Ed Davey to draw up new ideas between the main parties.



Mr Burnham speech in North London will reiterate that it is time to take the politics out of reforming social care.

He argued that squabbling in Westminster has led to “carers struggling, families paying the price and our NHS buckling under the strain”.



The Prime Minister said: “We can carry on passing the problem to the next generation, or we can face it head on and work together to build a care system that gives people dignity, security and the support they deserve.”

Mandarins led by Baroness Louise Casey are tasked with drawing up the skeleton of a new National Care Service.

A Big Conversation on Care forum will urge the public to share their views and shape the future of adult social care in England.

Punters are paying for a failed social care system by eye-watering council taxes, pressure on the NHS and giving up work, Baroness Casey argued.

She added: The choice is whether we keep putting money into a system that is unfair, unpredictable and broken, or have an honest conversation about how to build something better.

Mr Burnham has failed to rule out funding social care with a 10 per cent “death tax”.



Reform and the Tories have challenged Andy Burnham to rule out tax hikes to fix Britain’s broken social care system.

The Prime Minister has vowed he does not want to leave office without fixing the crisis, but has not explained how he would pay for any reform.

Reform UK claimed Mr Burnham’s touted new ‘death tax’ will cost the average mortgage-free Makerfield homeowner £50,669.

But a mortgage-free homeowner in England and Wales will have to stump up £74,737.

Reform’s Robert Jenrick said: “Andy Burnham has no mandate whatsoever to raid people’s precious savings.



“Voters have already rejected a death tax on four separate occasions and it flies in the face of his so-called ‘Makerfield Test’.”

Tory leader Ms Badenoch said she is willing to help Mr Burnham push through plans for social care but said he must not raise taxes to pay for it.

Writing to the Prime Minister, Tory leader Kemi Badenoch said: “The money must be found by reducing current spending. You must rule out any tax rises, or increased borrowing that will ultimately fall on the next generation to pay for.”

She added: “The last thing Britain needs is further tax increases to pay for social care.”

News.title: Iran launches ‘surprise’ missile strikes on US forces days after Trump pauses bombing to give diplomacy another chance
News.content:
SHOCK BLITZ Iran launches ‘surprise’ missile strikes on US forces days after Trump pauses bombing to give diplomacy another chance

IRAN has launched a fresh wave of ballistic missiles at US forces based in Jordan in an “attempted surprise attack”.

It marks the first blitz between Washington and Tehran since Donald Trump paused tit-for-tat strikes last week to resume negotiations.



All the missiles were intercepted, according to US Central Command (Centcom) on Tuesday.

They said: “At 5:45 p.m. ET today, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces launched multiple ballistic missiles from Iran in an attempted surprise attack on US forces based in the Middle East.



“All Iranian missiles were successfully intercepted.

“US forces remain vigilant and at a high state of readiness.”



Shocking footage showed missile interceptions lighting up the night sky as rockets were seen blowing up over Jordanian neighbourhoods.

Regime strikes could shatter the fragile ceasefire implemented by Trump on Friday.



The pause in fighting was aimed at letting talks continue to iron out a solid peace deal once and for all.

The US president threatened on Monday he would get back to “very strong military action” if negotiations fell through.

He told Axios he was in “very deep talks” with Iran.



Asked how long he was willing to give Tehran to finalise a peace deal, Trump said: “Not much time.”

He said: “Either it goes fast or not at all.”

Earlier this month in Jordan, two US service members were killed in a missile and drone barrage.

The deadly assaults caused Trump to intensify his two week-long blitz of the regime.

Trump’s decision to row back on planned strikes was caused by a diminished stockpile of Patriot antimissile interceptors, according to the New York Times.



On Friday, the warring nations were said to be keen on returning to an interim ceasefire deal, but Iran‘s control over the Strait of Hormuz remained a sticking point.

After being besieged for nearly four months, the Strait was reopened to commercial shipping after a memorandum of understanding (MOU) was signed on June 17.

There was hope that negotiators could hash out a deal, bringing an end to the brutal conflict and stabilising global fuel prices.

But that turned out to be a false dawn as Iran’s trigger-happy Islamic Guards began firing on ships in the strait.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

After two weeks of bombing throughout July, Trump is reportedly reluctant to keep widening the war.



An escalation risks alienating key Gulf allies who have been targeted by Iran, as well as a global economic crunch if the strait remains closed.

News.title: Creators of Farage guillotine t-shirt paraded at Zack Polanski Green Party festival remove it from sale
News.content:
THE creators of the Farage guillotine t-shirt paraded at a Zack Polanski Green Party festival last night removed it from sale.

Sabcat Printing were selling the £20 top showing the execution method with the words “We’re only making plans for Nigel”.



But the company – part of an “anarchist co-operative” based out of a warehouse in Manchester – claimed it was “satire”.

A picture of a clubber wearing the slogan at a Green Party rave in Bristol at the weekend was posted on social media and “liked” by leader Polanski.



It sparked a furious response from Reform UK boss Nigel Farage who demanded cops arrest his political rival.

It came in the wake of the recent horrific death of former MP Ann Widdecombe who was allegedly bludgeoned to death with a hammer by a left-wing activist.



Last night the makers of the t-shirt – a company founded by two men from Burntwood, Staffs – said it was not meant to be taken literally.

A man at the firm’s warehouse, who wished to be called “Steve the cleaner” told The Sun: “It is not for sale any more.

“It went on sale around spring but I took it off sale last night.

“It is a p***take. It is satire.



“Nigel Farage is always on about people wanting to kill him.

“Unfortunately it has got Zack Polanski into trouble.

“It is not inciting anything.



“It is not meant to be taken seriously.

“It is not a good time with Ann Widdecombe.

“Ann Widdecombe was an old lady and what happened is horrific and not on.

“If they want to legalise the guillotine that is up to them.



“We sold a few of the tee-shirts – a very small amount in dribs and drabs.

“It was probably less than 20 and we won’t be printing any more.

“I am not consumerist, we don’t do fast fashion.

“The other tee-shirts on sale are not offensive.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Some people are offended by anti-racism or anti-fascism.”



Mr Polanski deleted the picture yesterday after its contents were “brought to his attention” and insisted he “does not support this type of dangerous message”.

News.title: Man hikes 10 miles with walking pole speared through body after freak accident – as pals joke he ‘looks like a kebab’
News.content:
SKEWERED PLANS Man hikes 10 miles with walking pole speared through body after freak accident – as pals joke he ‘looks like a kebab’

A MAN hiked 10 miles with a trekking pole speared through his body after a freak accident on Montana’s highest mountain.

David Cifaldi slipped while climbing 12,803ft Granite Peak and fell onto one of his walking poles, which pierced his side before protruding from his lower back.



Instead of calling for rescue, the emergency room nurse calmly assessed his injuries and spent hours walking back down the mountain.

Recalling the terrifying moment, Cifaldi told KTVQ: “By the time I rolled over, I kind of knew something wasn’t right.”



The pole had entered below his left arm, exited through his lower back and narrowly missed several vital organs.

“Through my skin, I could feel the trekking pole,” he said.

“I knew it wasn’t deep, and I knew I could take deep breaths.”

His medical training quickly took over.



“I think my nurse brain clicked on,” Cifaldi told Montana’s Local 12.

“As soon as I was able to self-assess and establish that this was not life-threatening right now, I was pretty convinced I was going to get off that mountain under my own power.”

After reaching the trailhead, Cifaldi was taken to a nearby clinic before friends drove him two hours to a hospital in Billings, where surgeons carefully removed the pole.

“I feel very lucky,” he said.

“A couple inches the other way and this would be a different story.”



Cifaldi and friends Jesse Ross and Brad Reich had set off at 3.30am to climb Granite Peak and were just 1,000ft from the summit when disaster struck.

On the descent, one friend walked behind him to make sure he didn’t stumble on the rugged terrain, while the other went ahead to warn approaching hikers.

To keep spirits high, the two friends even “started making kebab jokes”.

A fundraiser has since been launched to help cover Cifaldi’s medical bills.

Ross wrote: “He self-assessed calmly: no bleeding, full feeling, no lightheadedness, nothing vital hit, and the pole stable in place.



“Given his condition, he made the call to self-rescue rather than wait for extraction – hiking 10 miles back to the trailhead with a trekking pole still through his body.

“He reached the trailhead entirely under his own power – never once complaining, staying in remarkably high spirits.”

Once fully recovered, Cifaldi says the trio plan to return and finally conquer the summit that nearly claimed his life.

Granite Peak is listed at between 12,799ft and 12,807ft, depending on the survey, making it Montana’s highest mountain.

First summited in 1923, only 17 climbers are known to have reached the top during the next three decades.



The remote peak is also the setting of one of American climbing’s greatest mysteries.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In 1959, Ernest Bruffey vanished during a solo ascent on the same day a powerful earthquake killed 28 people in Montana.

His fate remained a mystery for more than 40 years until a group of six friends discovered human remains in 2000.

News.title: Cops launch probe after aircraft engineer, 23, was crushed to death inside plane fuel tank at Heathrow Airport
News.content:
PLANE HORROR Cops launch probe after aircraft engineer, 23, was crushed to death inside plane fuel tank at Heathrow Airport

COPS have launched a probe after an airport engineer was crushed to death inside a plane fuel tank after machinery suddenly fell on him.

Georgie Buxton, 23, was in intensive care for over a month after the horrifying accident in a hangar at Heathrow Airport.



Earlier this month, his family took the heartbreaking decision to switch off his life support.

Georgie was carrying out maintenance tests on a Boeing 787 at around 8pm on June 11 when machinery suddenly collapsed on him.



The plane he was working on has been taken out of service since the accident while experts try to understand how the tragedy occurred.

A source told The Sun: “Georgie was a young and very loved member of the team. Everyone at Virgin is in shock.

“It was not immediately clear what caused the death, and officials have grounded the jet until further notice on safety grounds.

“Heavy metal cannot fall from a jet machinery and the plane be allowed to continue flying.”

A Virgin Atlantic spokesperson told The Sun: “We are heartbroken to confirm that a much-loved member of our engineering team has passed away.

“Our thoughts are firmly with Georgie’s family, loved ones, friends and colleagues at this incredibly sad and challenging time.



“We’re providing support to loved ones wherever we can and sharing our heartfelt condolences to everyone affected.

“Georgie’s family has asked for privacy at this very difficult time.

“The safety and wellbeing of our people is always our top priority, and we are devastated by this incident.

“We are working closely with relevant authorities and the aircraft manufacturer on the investigation to establish all facts.

“Out of respect for those involved and while the investigation is ongoing, we are unable to provide any further information at this stage.”



Virgin Atlantic boasts 17 Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, each carrying up to 264 passengers.

News.title: M1 closed after multi-car crash causes lorry to flip on its side and ‘substantial oil spillage’ – as cops rush to scene
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

'HORRIFIC ACCIDENT' M1 closed after multi-car crash causes lorry to flip on its side and ‘substantial oil spillage’ – as cops rush to scene

THE M1 has been partially closed after a horror multi-vehicle collision which caused a lorry to flip on its side and a “substantial oil spillage”.

The southbound section between Junction 12, for Toddington, and Junction 11, for Luton, has been shut.



The incident occurred shortly before 8:45pm on July 28.

One of the HGVs involved has overturned and come to rest on its side.



The nearside barrier and boundary fencing have suffered “significant damage” and a “substantial oil spillage” has affected most lanes, National Highways said.

Traffic that was caught within the closure has now been released past the scene via lane 4.

Bedfordshire Police and other emergency services remain in attendance.

National Highways traffic officers are also on scene assisting with traffic management.

The carriageway will remain closed while emergency services complete their response, followed by vehicle recovery, barrier repairs and carriageway clean-up.

National Highways has set up a diversion and drivers are advised to follow the hollow circle diversion symbol on road signs.



Up to the minute information can be got from National Highways contact centre team on 0300 123 5000.

News.title: Police seize fake World Cup shirts worth £18.5m in major crackdown
News.content:
Police seize fake World Cup shirts worth £18.5m in major crackdown

Officers have seized more them 220,000 fake shirts, with a genuine retail value at an estimated £18.5 million, since January 2026 in a nationwide enforcement operation

View 3 Images Officers have removed more than 220,000 fake shirts from sale since January 2026 (Image: City of London Police/PA Wire)

Counterfeit football shirts and kits worth more than £18 million have been seized over the course of the World Cup, the City of London Police have said.

Officers have removed more them 220,000 fake shirts from sale since January 2026 in a nationwide enforcement operation led by the force’s Police Intellectual Property Crime Unit (Pipcu). The total genuine retail value was estimated at £18.5 million, the force said.

Four people were also arrested on suspicion of selling counterfeit shirts, and a further two arrests were made by other police forces. The City of London Police said their operation focused on online marketplaces and live shopping apps as well as traditional market stalls as offenders increasingly use tech platforms to sell counterfeit goods.

View 3 Images Harry Kane looks dejected after the FIFA World Cup 2026 Semi Final match between England and Argentina (Image: Julian Finney - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Woman found dead at remote cottage in Renfrewshire was murdered, police say READ MORE :

Counterfeit shirts are produced in unsafe and unregulated conditions and can contain harmful materials that fail safety standards, while profits from the sales are used to fund criminal operations, police warned.

Detective Chief Inspector Amanda Lowe, head of Pipcu, said: “Counterfeit football shirts aren’t a harmless bargain, they are a key revenue stream for organised crime groups, helping to mask and fund the criminality happening behind the scenes.

“As World Cup fever began to build, partners across the country came together to tackle this ever-growing issue. Our aim was simple; to ensure fans enjoyed the tournament and supporting their team in a shirt that’s safe and legitimate. “An issue of this scale demands a coordinated response, and we’ll continue working with our law enforcement, Government and industry partners to crack down on this illegal trade and the criminals who drive it.” City of London Police have also warned the sale of counterfeit goods deprives rights holders and legitimate businesses of revenue, while putting buyers’ personal data at risk and exposing them to financial fraud. “This is anything but a victimless crime,” Helen Barnham, head of enforcement engagement at the Intellectual Property Office, said. “The trade in counterfeit goods is estimated to cost thousands of jobs in the UK each year and supports other forms of serious crime – harming legitimate businesses, society and the wider economy.”

A spokesperson from the Football Association further warned fans: “We would strongly advise all fans to avoid counterfeit products. Not only are such products often poor quality but brand abuse and counterfeiting negatively impacts the FA’s role as a not-for-profit organisation that directly funds all levels of our national game.”

View 3 Images Football fans have been warned about the fake shifts (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Things to look out for

Buyers trying to assess whether a football shirt is fake have been advised to check the price, as what looks like a bargain may turn out to be a scam. If possible, they should also inspect the shirt’s quality by looking out for poor stitching – especially around the neckline and badge – low-quality fabric and a bad fit.

They should also ensure logos and tags match the manufacturer, and check that the swing tag includes a unique product code sticker and product-specific wording.

Handwritten numbers on care labels are also a sign the shirt may be a counterfeit product.

Fans can also purchase from official retailers or the club’s store, verify website security, and be cautious of sites using official product photos without clear retailer credentials.

This follows reports that football fans face paying up to £90 for replica shirts after eight Premier League clubs increased their prices – raising concerns fans may be left priced out of buying their favourite kit.

Tottenham fans must now pay £90 for a replica adult first-team shirt, up £5 on last year, while a shirt for a child as young as three years old now costs £70, according to the club’s website. A shirt for just-promoted Coventry City is up £10 to £70 and the club’s children’s shirts are also up, by 25% to £60, while a baby kit costs £55.

Article continues below

Chelsea has also increased the price of its shirts by £5 to £89.99, while Ipswich Town shirts are up £6 to £65. Leeds, Bournemouth and Hull shirts are all £5 more expensive than last year.

Consumer expert Scott Dixon, from The Complaints Resolver, said on Monday: “These price rises will leave many loyal fans wondering when enough is enough. We see this year in, year out, and it smacks of blatant greed and an own goal that could backfire on clubs. These kits are overpriced by anyone’s standards and will leave many fans priced out.”

News.title: France wildfires live: 184 arsonists arrested as 'all regions' at risk of further fires
News.content:
Flames are nearing the French Atlantic Coast with raging wildfires now nine miles from Bordeaux as the city's mayor says he's prepared for 'all eventualities'

All regions of France are potentially at risk of wildfires tomorrow as the country grapples with what President Macron has claimed is the "most difficult situation" his country has dealt with since World War Two.

“We are facing two particularly critical days, with the heatwave and the very dry forest,” Gironde mayor Blandine Sarrazin. told local media. "This is the third fire to start here in the last two and a half days, it's really difficult," she added, telling residents it was not yet safe to return home.

Holidaymakers have been forced to leave campsites, tourist homes, holiday villages and leisure parks around Lacanau, which is around 40 miles from Bordeaux. The order comes as firefighters race against time to bring the fires under control before the country's south-west is blasted by a forecast 40C heatwave tomorrow (Wednesday).

Officials say the largest blaze has "stabilised" but have warned it could still burn out of control again as temperatures rise and humidity falls.

But a number of additional fires continue to burn with no end in sight, as local officials warn that the inferno could continue for months before it is fully contained.

France's Interior Minister Laurent Nunez claimed wildfire season is "far from over," and said authorities have arrested 1 84 suspected arsonists since the start of the summer.

Meanwhile in Spain, 63,000 people have been evacuate from their homes near Madrid, with the country's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez calling it "the most painful expression of the climate emergency".

News.title: Japan earthquake live: Dozens still missing as search for survivors continues overnight
News.content:
Multiple people have died while more are missing after a shopping centre collapsed following a huge 7.1 magnitude earthquake on the Japanese island of Kyushu

Dozens of people are still reported missing following the horror collapse of a shopping mall in Japan that caused 'many fatalities' after being struck by a powerful earthquake.

Up to 30 others remain missing at the Aeon Mall in Kumamoto, while employees are also missing at the nearby Nippon Paper Industries Yatsushiro Plant. Several people travelling in a high speed train were also injured after a chimney stack from the paper company fell on them during the quake, local media reports.

“People are coming in with burns and fractures from being trapped under objects due to the earthquake, and ambulances are constantly bringing in injured people,” a hospital employee told national broadcaster NHK.

“Inside the hospital, there are water leaks and electrical system failures,” they added.

The massive quake measured at the highest possible level seven on Japan's own Shindo "scale of shaking" and has left tens of thousands without power. Kumamoto Airport has been closed indefinitely after the earthquake rocked its runway.

Kumamoto was hit with a deadly quake in 2016 that left more than 50 people dead, 1,800 injured and tens of thousands of homes damaged or destroyed.

News.title: Woman found dead at remote cottage in Renfrewshire was murdered, police say
News.content:
Woman found dead at remote cottage in Renfrewshire was murdered, police say

Stacy Mair, 35, was found dead at a remote cottage in Renfrewshire by emergency services after reports of concern for a person on Monday morning - police are now treating it as murder

View 3 Images Stacy Mair, who was found deceased on Monday at around 7.50am in the Corsliehill Road area of Houston (Image: Family Handout/PA Wire)

Police are treating the death of a woman found in a remote cottage as murder, while the death of a man at the scene is being treated as "unexplained".

‌



The body of 35-year-old Stacy Mair and a 43-year-old man were discovered by emergency services at Corsliehill Road in Houston, Johnstone on Monday morning, July 27, following reports of a concern for a person.

‌



Police Scotland initially said the deaths were being treated as unexplained, but they have now confirmed they believe Stacy may have been murdered. A post-mortem will be carried out to establish the exact cause of death in due course.

‌



View 3 Images Police officers near to the scene in Houston, Johnstone, Renfrewshire (Image: Ryan McDougall/PA Wire)

A Police Scotland spokesperson said: "Death of 35-year-old Stacy Mair in Houston being treated as murder. Around 7.50am on Monday, 27 July, 2026, we received a report of concern for a person in the Corsliehill Road area of Houston.

"Emergency services attended, and the bodies of a woman and a man were found nearby. Following a post-mortem examination today, the death of 35-year-old Stacy Mair is being treated as murder.

‌



"The death of the 43-year-old man continues to be treated as unexplained pending the results of a post-mortem examination, which will take place in due course. Detectives from Police Scotland's Major Investigation Team, as well as officers from the local policing division, continue to carry out extensive enquiries to establish the full circumstances.

"At this time, there is nothing to suggest anyone else is involved or any risk to the public."

Detective Chief Inspector Laura Young, of the Major Investigation Team, said: "Our thoughts remain with the families of those affected by this incident. They are understandably devastated, and we are providing them with support through specialist officers at this incredibly difficult time."

‌



View 3 Images The bodies of a man and a woman have been found in what police have described as "unexplained" circumstances (Image: Ryan McDougall/PA Wire)

Chief Inspector Iain Farmer said: "This is a deeply upsetting incident for the families involved, and the impact is felt right across the local community. I am grateful for the support we have received as we complete our essential enquires to ensure the families and local residents get the answers they need.”

"Anyone with concerns or information can contact Police Scotland via 101."

‌



Photos taken by the Record at the scene on Tuesday show multiple police vehicles parked outside a property in Houston and a nearby road. Officers can be seen by the cottage where vans are also stationed in an adjacent field as well as scouring nearby woodland.

The home sits on the main road, with another similar style of property situated just a few hundred yards away.

Corsliehill Road is a narrow rural lane surrounded by farmland and a handful of isolated properties, with little passing traffic. Reports suggest a significant emergency services response was seen in the area with a police helicopter also present on Monday.

Article continues below

The Scottish Ambulance Service has confirmed it received a call at 8.33am and sent four special operations response teams, two ambulances and a critical care team to the scene. A Scottish Ambulance Service spokesperson said: “We received a call at 08.33 to attend an incident on Barochan Road, Houston, Johnstone. Four special operations response teams (SORT), two ambulances and one critical care team were dispatched to the scene.”

News.title: Death row inmate's chilling last two words before double execution in Florida
News.content:
Death row inmate's chilling last two words before double execution in Florida

James Aren Duckett, 68, was confirmed dead early on Tuesday in the wake of a lethal injection cocktail of three drugs at Florida state prison near Starke

View 3 Images James Aren Duckett has now been put to death (Image: Florida Department of Corrections)

A former policeman has been put to death, nearly 40 years after he raped and murdered 11-year-old Teresa McAbee while he was working as an officer in central Florida in 1987. James Aren Duckett, 68, was confirmed dead early on Tuesday in the wake of a lethal injection cocktail of three drugs at Florida state prison near Starke. Duckett is the 11th inmate to be executed by the state in 2026. When asked, he declined to make a final statement and instead chose to respond with “no sir” when asked.

Four minutes later, he was shaken by a prison warden who also shouted Duckett's name, but the rapist and murderer was unresponsive.

View 3 Images Florida State Prison (Image: Douglas R Clifford/Tampa Bay Times/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Hours later, the State of Florida then went on to execute 80-year-old Dominick Occhicone tonight at Florida State Prison, completing the state’s first same-day double execution in over 60 years following the noon execution of Duckett.

Florida has now also put to death its second man in one day for the 1986 double murder of Raymond and Martha Artzner, the parents of his ex-girlfriend, Anita Gerrety.

At around 3am on June 10, 1986, Occhicone knocked on the door of his ex’s parents' Pasco County home. As per court records, he wished to rekindle their relationship, court records show. He left when Anita threatened to call the sheriff.

He returned an hour later and this time, he came with lethal intent. Anita’s father Raymond tried to call the sheriff's office, but the phone line had been cut at the junction box, prosecutors said.

Occhicone then shot Anita’s father Raymond in the face. As per the Herald-Tribune, Occhicone then broke through a locked door and chased his ex through the house, but she was able to get outside with her daughter, she later testified.

She heard gunshots ring out behind her and her mother, Martha Artzner, was later found dead.

Raymond Artzner lived long enough to tell deputies who shot him but died at the hospital, prosecutors said. Occhicone did not deny the evidence later in court, but argued the shootings were not premeditated. He was not believed by a jury of his peers, and has been on death row ever since.

But now, 40 years after the brutal revenge slaying of his ex’s parents, Occhicone’s execution has finally gone ahead after forward after the Florida Supreme Court unanimously rejected all of his final appeals earlier on in the week.

Occhicone therefore became the oldest person executed in modern history in Florida and the second-oldest put to death in the US after the 2018 execution of Walter Moody, who was executed at age 83.

View 3 Images Dominick Anthony Occhicone is dead by lethal injection (Image: Florida Department of Correction)

Occhicone’s death came six hours after the execution of 68-year-old Duckett at noon.

The double executions day is Florida's first since 1964, when Blake Emmett and Dawson Sie were both executed in the electric chair. The last time any state carried out two executions in one day was back in 2017, when Arkansas held back-to-back executions.

Article continues below

Florida’s Republican governor Ron DeSantis has made his state’s death chamber the busiest in the US as the end of his final term approaches. DeSantis has previously said too many families have waited too long to see justice, hence the uptick in lethal injections. Nationwide, the death penalty had been on the decline for more than 20 years. That number has now tracked back upwards behind the increased pace set in Florida. Since 2025, Florida has carried out nearly half the state executions across the US.

News.title: More than 200 wildfires across England and Wales in 12 days as 'risk remains elevated across UK'
News.content:
More than 200 wildfires across England and Wales in 12 days as 'risk remains elevated across UK'

More than 700 wildfires have so far been recorded this year across England and Wales, with the figures not accounting for blazes such as the one in Cairngorms, Scotland

View 3 Images Firefighters in Derbyshire continue to make progress at a major wildfire at Tintwistle Moor (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The risk of wildfires "remains elevated across the UK" as more than 200 incidents have been recorded in the last 12 days.

‌



If fires started in London, the South East or East of England during the heatwave, the blazes could be exceptionally severe due to the hot, dry conditions. An amber heat-health alert has been issued again by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) covering the East Midlands, the East and South East of England and London.

‌



The warning came into force today and will stay in place until Thursday, with the hot temperatures posing a threat to health risks, particularly for those in vulnerable age groups like the elderly. A total of 706 wildfires were reported to fire and rescue services across England and Wales so far this year.

‌



Of those, 208 incidents were recorded in less than a fortnight, between July 16 and 28, the National Fire Chiefs Council (NFCC) said. The figures, however, do not account for wildfires across Scotland and Northern Ireland.

View 3 Images The fire burning through the Cairngorms national park in northern Scotland (Image: RSPB Scotland/AFP via Getty Images)

This means blazes like the one in Cairngorms in Scotland, which firefighters have been battling for two weeks now, were not included in the statistics. The incident, which saw families being ordered to leave their homes, shows "how quickly wildfire activity can increase during prolonged periods of hot and dry weather".

‌



Fire chiefs warned that wildfire risks "remains elevated across the UK", as NFCC explained eight live wildfire incidents are currently being monitored. Firefighters in Derbyshire continue to "make progress at the major wildfire incident at Tintwistle Moor", where 60 crew members were sent today.

Still, figures across England and Wales remain lower than the 788 recorded by this time last year. However, NFCC warned that "continued dry conditions, combined with warmer temperatures and harvesting activity in many rural areas" were creating conditions in which fires can start and spread rapidly.

Images showed widespread brown grass across Blackheath in London, with parched dry grass present in many parks in the capital following the hot weather. It comes as Royal Parks staff were advised not to leave deckchairs under trees over fears branches will fall during hot weather.

‌



View 3 Images A French Civil Security aircraft flying over an area affected by a fire at Camp de Souge Martignas-sur-Jalle, near Bordeaux (Image: SDIS33/MATTHIEU PENZ HANDOUT/EPA/Shutterstock)

Countries across Europe are also burning as large-scale wildfires have hit parts of Spain, France, Greece and Italy. This led to evacuations and significant damage, along with sustained pressure on emergency services, who are now struggling to fight the enormity of the fires.

The NFCC said UK wildfires are typically smaller and different in nature to those seen in southern Europe, adding, however, that the "long-term effects of climate change are increasing the likelihood of larger, more complex and more resource-intensive wildfire incidents occurring".

‌



Phil Garrigan, chairman of the NFCC, said: "More than 200 wildfires in just 12 days shows how quickly the risk can escalate when hot, dry conditions take hold. The scenes we’re seeing across parts of Europe are a stark reminder of what a changing climate means for fire and rescue services.

"We are not seeing fires of that scale in the UK today, but the science tells us we should expect larger, more frequent and more complex wildfires in the future. That’s why we need continued investment in specialist wildfire capabilities, including aerial firefighting support, so we’re prepared for the risks ahead.

"But prevention remains our strongest defence. Most wildfires are avoidable, and we’re asking everyone to take extra care during the hot weather to help keep their communities safe."

Article continues below

Fire chiefs said many wildfires are caused by everyday human activity, adding that "disposing of cigarettes safely, avoiding the use of disposable barbecues in open spaces and taking litter home can significantly reduce the risk of fires starting". This month has been 3C above average across the UK, provisional Met Office data shows.

This means July 2026 could be among the hottest three or four months of July on record.

News.title: Manchester Airport emergency as firefighters surround Turkish Airline flight
News.content:
Manchester Airport emergency as firefighters surround Turkish Airline flight

Airport officials have confirmed that all passengers disembarked safely after the flight was diverted after a 'technical issue'

View 2 Images Fire service vehicles at Manchester Airport today (July 28) (Image: Liam Smith)

A Turkish Airlines flight has been forced to make an emergency landing at Manchester Airport (July 28). Flight THY1GJ was travelling from Istanbul to Toronto but diverted to Manchester Airport to land at around 7:30pm after doing some laps over the North Sea. As per flight data, the plane likely had to dump fuel in order to land. The plane was met by multiple airport fire and rescue vehicles on arrival, but touched down without incident. Airport officials confirmed the technical issue was addressed, and all passengers disembarked normally.

‌



View 2 Images The Toronto-bound plane made an emergency landing. (Image: Liam Smith)

A spokesperson for Manchester Airport said the aircraft had landed safely and had a 'technical issue' that had since been resolved. Turkish Airlines have been contacted for more information.

News.title: Andrew Tate's lawyer reveals how he tweets despite being locked in solitary confinement
News.content:
Andrew Tate's lawyer reveals how he tweets despite being locked in solitary confinement

A lawyer representing Andrew Tate has revealed that he jots down messages from the social media influencer when they meet at jail and then posts them online

View 3 Images Andrew Tate, right, and his brother Tristan pictured in April in Miami (Image: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP via A)

Andrew Tate's lawyer has told how the social media influencer posts messages online despite being in jail.

It was revealed yesterday that he and his brother Tristan will remain in jail for at least two more weeks until their next hearing as they fight extradition to the United Kingdom - where the brothers are accused of multiple counts of rape and sex trafficking, a federal judge said.

US magistrate Lauren Louis set a detention hearing for August 13 to determine whether the pair should stay in jail or be released during what could be a months-long extradition process.

The Tates were not in court on Monday or required to be there and have remained in jail since making a brief court appearance two days after their July 18 arrest.

View 3 Images Joseph McBride revealed how Andrew Tate tweets from prison (Image: Getty Images)

But it is now clear how Andrew Tate has been sending out messages while in solitary confinement as his lawyers jot down his opinions when they meet to discuss his case.

“Look, we meet with Andrew every day, we see Andrew,” attorney Joseph McBride told the New York Post outside court.

“I see Andrew four, five, six times a week. So we’re in there, we’re out of there, you know, it’s called the Pony Express. There’s a way to be like, ‘What would you like said to the world?’ It’s not very hard.”

And McBride added: “Of course not, no”, when asked if Andrew Tate had access to a phone at FDC Miami. “If he had a phone in there, they’d probably give him the electric chair,” he joked.

While the lawyer also responded to Andrew Tate's claim that his “neighbour” in the detention centre is a cannibal. “I don’t know his name, we just know him as Mr. Cannibal,” McBride told reporters.

“He screams all night. He’s got deep issues. We don’t know if they’re emotional, if they’re demonic or what’s going on but, you know, if you’re a cannibal, you’ve got problems — objectively.”

On July 23, Tate’s X account posted, “I am being held in [the special housing unit], the highest level of security which exists. No commissary. No visits. No contact with the outside world. My neighbour is a cannibal who screams throughout the night.”

Meanwhile, lawyers for the brothers said yesterday that they want the US government to turn over documents that UK officials submitted to secure their arrest in the States.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

“They don’t have anything but the accusations,” attorney Joseph McBride said after the hearing. “It’s just their word against our word right now.”

The UK has until mid-September to turn over all of its materials to the State Department, US attorney Alejandra Lopez said in court. The brothers have long claimed that their violent and misogynistic statements have been taken out of context or were intended as jokes.

Jackie Perczek, another one of their lawyers, said the Tates have shown they are not a flight risk by returning to Romania every month after they were accused there of luring women for sexual exploitation.

“For three years they have not fled,” she said. “They’ve travelled the world and every month they return to Romania.”

View 3 Images Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan (L) are facing dozens of charges of rape, trafficking and assault. (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The former professional kickboxers, who have dual US and UK citizenship, have millions of social media followers and are vocal supporters of Donald Trump. The White House has said the brothers shouldn’t expect any help from the president.

McBride said shortly after the Tates were arrested that “they’ve never done nothing wrong. They shouldn’t be extradited for crimes they did not commit,” he said. McBride said the extradition attempt was politically motivated, though he provided no details.

Article continues below

Prosecutors in Britain said the new charges relate to four new accusers and were brought after authorities received evidence from police in Bedfordshire. The allegations, which span from 2010 to 2017, include rape, assault, trafficking and offences relating to “indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.”

The brothers are already charged with rape, bodily harm, human trafficking and controlling prostitution for gain relating to three other accusers in the UK between 2012 and 2015.

The brothers moved to Romania in 2016 and were arrested there in 2022, accused of participating in schemes to lure women for sexual exploitation. They denied those allegations, and the Romanian case hasn’t gone forward because of legal and procedural problems.

News.title: The moment Tuesday's powerful earthquake hit Japan
News.content:
A powerful earthquake struck Japanâs Kyushu island on 28 July, forcing more than 150,000 people to evacuate. The quake caused power outages, damaged roads, brought down part of a castle wall, and destroyed a footbridge. More than 40,000 households are without power and several people are missing after a chimney collapsed at a paper factory in the Kumamoto prefecture, according to the police who are being cited by Japan's public broadcaster NHK.

News.title: Some parents on benefits to get up to £4,500 for child starting apprenticeship
News.content:
Some parents on benefits will be given up to Â£4,500 a year to encourage their children to start apprenticeships, the government has said.

Under plans to encourage young people into work, families will be offered a bursary to replace Universal Credit payments lost by starting jobs.

The payment is expected to benefit an estimated few thousand households, who currently face losing between Â£17 and Â£330 a week if their children start apprenticeships.

The Conservatives welcomed Prime Minister Andy Burnham's support for apprenticeships, but criticised his plans to fund the bursaries.

The bursary will be paid for from a Â£30m pot, funded through the growth and skills levy, a tax on employers with annual wage bills over Â£3m.

It followed the publication of a Social Security Advisory Committee report, external which warned of the "perverse effects" of the benefits system on young people's employment choices.

It said, for example, single parents with a disabled child could lose up to Â£340 per week in benefits if their child started an apprenticeship, exceeding the expected apprenticeship salary of Â£258 per week.

Because they are classed as paid employment, benefit payments are reduced to households where young people take on apprenticeships.

The committee said the system was hampering government efforts to reduce the number of young people not in education, employment or training (Neet).

In a recent report, former Health Secretary Alan Milburn warned that one in six young people could be Neet in the next five years unless urgent action is taken.

Official figures show more than a million people aged 16 to 24 are currently Neet.

The government said its new bursary would remove a barrier to young people taking on apprenticeships, allowing them to "earn and learn".

Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden said: "By providing bursaries to those who need them most and fully funding apprenticeship training, we are making sure cost is not the reason someone misses out."

It is part of a wider package of support for apprenticeships, including funding for apprenticeship training for under-25s and additional support for employers taking on apprentices.

Helen Whately, the Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary, said: "I'm glad Burnham agrees: apprenticeships are a good thing, and we need more of them."

But she said the plan was "uncosted".

"It is spending money already committed elsewhere. So, either it is another unfunded announcement, or Andy Burnham is not being straight with us about his plans."

Burnham has said he is "on a mission" to reduce the number of Neets.

"The trend is rising at the moment, so the first thing I've got to do is to stop that rise," he said.

As he continues a flurry of early policy announcements, Burnham on Tuesday set out plans to strike a balance in the education system between prioritising academic and technical skills.

News.title: The evidence that shows today's 20-somethings really do have it worse
News.content:
Young people in their 20s are facing a tougher start to adulthood than any generation in almost half a century, according to analysis of UK data on housing, employment and wealth, carried out for the BBC.

More than 40% of 25-year-olds are now living with their parents, their wages have stagnated and employment has fallen, show the figures which compare key metrics for different generations at age 25 stretching back to the early 1980s.

The findings are underscored by the experiences of young people themselves who, along with parents, have contacted BBC Your Voice about their circumstances, with many saying they were frustrated about being accused by older generations of not trying hard enough.

We asked the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) to gather and analyse government data, external, for the first time, to see if this generation really does have it worse.

The biggest change it found was where those in their 20s are living.

News.title: Iran launches 'attempted surprise attack' on US forces in Middle East
News.content:
Iran has launched "multiple" ballistic missiles in an "attempted surprise attack" on American forces in the Middle East, the US military says, shattering a lull in the fighting.

The attack occurred at 17:45 EDT (21:45 GMT) on Tuesday, and all missiles were "successfully intercepted", said US Central Command, without specifying the locations of any targets.

Tehran has not yet commented. The alleged assault occurred during a break in hostilities between the two countries, which was designed to bring negotiators back to the table.

US President Donald Trump spoke on Monday of "very friendly negotiations" with Iran, after the two sides had not exchanged strikes for a third straight day.

"I think there's a good chance that something could happen," Trump added.

But he had also cautioned that the US could "go back to doing what we were doing" before the break in hostilities.

Access and control of the Strait of Hormuz remains a key sticking point in the talks.

News.title: Amber heat health alerts to come into force as heatwave reaches 35C peak
News.content:
Amber and yellow heat health alerts are set to come into force on Wednesday as parts of the UK endure the fourth widespread heatwave of the year so far.

Temperatures are forecast to peak at midweek with readings as high as 35C (95F) in the hottest places.

Though the heatwave will come to a quick end for many on Thursday, well above-average temperatures in the mid- to high 20s Celsius will persist into the weekend.

The hot weather, paired with a significant lack of rainfall, will exacerbate conditions in many of the driest areas.

News.title: Brits urged to avoid dangerous plug adaptors this summer - what to watch out for
News.content:
Brits going on holiday abroad this summer have been warned to watch out for dangerous travel adaptors, after an investigation suggested thousands may be for sale online.

Consumer safety group Electrical Safety First (ESF) tested 14 products from AliExpress, Amazon Marketplace, eBay and TikTok Shop - and found they all failed to meet UK safety requirements.

It said in some instances the devices could expose users to risk of serious electric shock or electrocution.

AliExpress, Amazon, eBay and TikTok all said they had removed the products ESF flagged from sale, and that they treated product safety as a top priority.

But Giuseppe Capanna, ESF product safety engineer, urged those "heading abroad this summer to think before they buy".

"What looks like a bargain could come at a much higher cost," he warned.

Capanna also said shoppers should buy travel adaptors from trusted retailers "so they can travel with confidence".

ESF tested six regular travel adaptors and eight universal adaptors it suspected could pose safety concerns.

To be sold in the UK, adaptors must not have accessible live parts and only one set of pins should come out at a time.

But the charity found multiple sets could be exposed simultaneously in six out of eight of the universal adaptors it tested.

None of the eight met the required dimensions and mechanical strength, while some pins snapped off under force during tests.

ESF said anyone who tried to remove a broken pin from a socket would be at risk of electric shock.

News.title: French Navy carries out 'shooting drill' during MP's BBC interview
News.content:
A French Navy patrol boat appeared to fire a round of gunshots "without warning" in the English Channel during a BBC interview with the UK shadow home secretary.

Conservative MP Chris Philp was being interviewed about small boat crossings by BBC journalist Michael Keohan as a French warship passed by at 09:15 BST (10:15 CET), about three miles from the French coast.

Keohan said there were 17 shots but "no warnings" from the boat about 300m away, which left Philp believing it was an intimidation tactic to "stop us covering migrant crossings".

The French authorities said it was part of a training exercise, unrelated to the presence of a British ship, which it said was out of range of fire.

Philp dismissed this claim as "not credible", adding: "There were no warnings in place about live firing training exercises.

"It looked and sounded exactly like deliberate intimidation."

News.title: Grieving mum was told baby's ashes were animal remains
News.content:
Ness suffered a miscarriage just before she was due to have her 12-week scan on April 20 2021.

She told how she had treasured the ashes for three years.

"They had sat on my shelf next to my baby scan," said Ness.

In court, prosecutor Chris Paxton KC said "the ashes that Lucy was given could not have been those of her baby".

The barrister did not state that they were of animal origin.

Ness was clear to the BBC, however, that police had told her the ashes were animal remains.

Her disgust at Bush was clear.

She said: "How can somebody with a duty of care do this to my family?"

She and her partner, Callum Ellerby, were told their baby was cremated on 10 May 2021.

"We didn't know the gender," said Ness. "We were not going to know the gender."

The day after the cremation was meant to have taken place, Bush, from Legacy Independent Funeral Directors, rang her and asked her to collect the ashes, which she did.

They were contained in a white china urn with a teddy bear embossed on it, Ness recalled.

When Humberside Police announced they were investigating Legacy in March 2024, Ness rang the helpline set up for anyone concerned.

The force then contacted her to say the ashes she had in her home could not be that of her baby, she said.

Officers explained to Ness that they had checked records at the crematorium and found Bush collected the baby's ashes on 13 May - two days after he had presented Ness and Ellerby with the urn.

She said: "I have felt very up and down. This has definitely impacted on my mental health."

News.title: Naga Munchetty to leave BBC Breakfast after 17 years
News.content:
Munchetty, 51, is among the best-paid presenters on the BBC's star salaries list, earning about Â£360,000 a year, according to the latest accounts.

She has interviewed major celebrities and politicians on the programme over the years ranging from Hillary Clinton and Michelle Obama to Sir Keir Starmer, Sir David Attenborough and Sir Rod Stewart.

In 2016, she appeared on the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing.

She has also been at the centre of some controversies during her time on BBC Breakfast.

In 2019, she was initially found to have breached the BBC's guidelines over comments she made about a social media post from Donald Trump about four female politicians of colour.

However, the BBC's director general then reversed that finding after deciding her words were not "sufficient to merit" upholding part of the complaint.

In 2021, Munchetty and co-presenter Charlie Stayt were "spoken to and reminded of their responsibilities" after complaints about their reaction to a government minister's flag. Munchetty apologised for liking "offensive" tweets about the exchange.

In June 2025, the Sun reported details of two alleged incidents which the paper said caused BBC bosses to speak to Munchetty about her conduct.

That came amid reports of behind-the-scenes tensions on the show, and at the same time as the programme's editor Richard Frediani took extended leave following allegations about his behaviour.

Frediani returned to work two weeks later and remains editor of BBC Breakfast.

At the time, the BBC said it did not comment on individual cases but took all complaints about conduct at work extremely seriously. Munchetty and Frediani did not comment on the reports.

The programme won a Bafta TV Award last year for best news coverage for a special about the Post Office scandal.

News.title: Laughter and tears at Dame Penelope Keith funeral
News.content:
Dame Penelope Keith's funeral has been hailed as "wonderful, beautiful and absolutely amazing" by her friends.

The actress, who starred in The Good Life and To The Manor Born, "died peacefully whilst living with cancer at her home" on 29 June at the age of 86.

Crowds lined the streets to say their goodbyes to the "very special lady" as her coffin travelled through her home town of Milford in Surrey before the service at Guildford Cathedral.

Broadcaster, writer and former politician Gyles Brandreth said the funeral was "filled with a mixture of sadness but laughter and gratitude as well because we were celebrating a great actress".

"It was a wonderful way to remember a remarkable person," he told BBC Radio Surrey.

Posting on X later, he said: "There was laughter and tears at Guildford Cathedral this morning - a truly beautiful and deeply moving funeral service for Dame Penelope Keith - what a lady and what a perfect service.

"It caught her completely. She was very special."

News.title: Unsolved Suzy Lamplugh case 'haunts' detectives
News.content:
Police officers investigating the disappearance of estate agent Suzy Lamplugh in west London say they remain "haunted" by the case, four decades after she went missing.

Lamplugh, 25, vanished after leaving her Fulham office to meet a client on the afternoon of 28 July 1986. She never returned and her body has never been found.

As the Metropolitan Police investigation is due to be mothballed next year, cold case detectives say they are troubled by the continuing mystery.

To mark the 40th anniversary of her disappearance, the Lamplugh family has released previously unseen photographs featuring her siblings Lizzie, Tamsin and Richard and her parents Paul and Diana.

In releasing the intimate family images, her siblings described her as "a truly beautiful person inside and out".

News.title: Two-Michelin-star chef brings fine dining to town football club
News.content:
Football fans will have the chance to swap their traditional match day pint and pie for a pop-up dining experience created by a renowned two-Michelin-star chef.

Gareth Ward, the chef behind Ynyshir Restaurant and Rooms near Machynlleth, Powys - which has an almost Â£500 per head tasting menu - has partnered up with Aberystwyth Town Football Club, in Ceredigion.

The collaboration will bring supporters different match day dining experiences, hospitality packages and corporate events throughout the season.

Ward, who has featured as a guest judge on MasterChef: The Professionals, said he was "excited" for the new venture.

The chef-patron said football clubs should be at "the heart of their communities".

The club's team is in the Novira Cymru South division, the second tier of Welsh football.

He added: "I see a real opportunity to bring people together through food and unforgettable matchday experiences and corporate events."

News.title: Schools to offer technical subjects to pupils from age 14 in England, Burnham says
News.content:
Secondary school pupils in England will be able to study subjects like manufacturing and AI in addition to core academic learning under reforms outlined by Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

The government said the courses, which would be available from Year 10, would be linked to local industries and designed to give children a clearer pathway into work.

Data published this year showed more than one million young people across the UK were not in education, employment or training, the highest level in more than 12 years.

Few details have been published about how the new vocational courses would work in practice and it is not clear how they would operate in areas with low industrial activity.

The BBC understands that the government expects the new pathways into work to be up and running in some areas by 2028.

Later on Tuesday, the government also announced a new bursary of up to Â£4,500 for some families who would lose out on money if their children wanted to do an apprenticeship, because the child benefit they would lose out on would be worth more than the apprenticeship starter salary.

Speaking at a train manufacturing site in Derby, Burnham said: "We've had a system built for too long around the university route and it sends a message to some young people that they're some kind of second-class citizens, and it's just not right.

"They need an education system that works for them as well, that offers a path to all young people, that's balanced between academic and technical."

The prime minister said he was "on a mission" to reduce the number of young people not in education, employment or training - known as "Neet" - but declined to put a target date on his ambition.

"The trend is rising at the moment, so the first thing I've got to do is to stop that rise," he said.

"It's hard to put a firm date on the moment when you can say there are fewer than now."

However, shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said while there was a "broad consensus" on improving vocational education, it was "not a big bold announcement".

She told BBC Breakfast: "What's going on there is a drastic shortage of jobs because Labour's policies over the last couple of years have killed job opportunities for young people. This announcement will not solve that."

News.title: Hundreds of thousands of women get morning-after pill via free pharmacy service
News.content:
The morning-after pill, known as emergency contraception, external, is medication designed to prevent unwanted pregnancies. It usually has to be taken within three to five days of having unprotected sex. The sooner it is taken, the more effective it is.

It works by delaying or preventing the release of an egg, but will only prevent pregnancy if ovulation has not already happened.

Alternatively, women can visit a doctor or nurse to have a coil or intrauterine device (IUD) fitted to prevent pregnancy at any time during their menstrual cycle. To be effective, it needs to be fitted within 120 hours or five days of unprotected sex.

The government said making the morning-after pill available free from pharmacies would end the "unfair" barriers and postcode lottery some women faced - with access varying dramatically depending on where they live.

Under the scheme, women can visit their local pharmacy and have a confidential consultation with a pharmacist or trained pharmacy technician, before receiving the medication on the same day.

Prior to this, women had to book an appointment with their GP, sexual health clinic or pharmacy to get the morning-after pill. Women could also access it privately, as they still can now.

In 2024/25, there were around 150,000 NHS prescriptions for the morning-after pill - far fewer than under the new service.

Dr Sue Mann, NHS National Clinical Director for Women's Health, said the pharmacy service was a "major step forward for women's health", with "no appointment, no waiting and no judgement".

"This service is already making a real impact, particularly for women living in more deprived communities, by making contraception easier to access closer to home," she added.

Women can check online, external to find their nearest participating pharmacy. All pharmacists and pharmacy technicians delivering the service have received specialist training to provide emergency contraception and wider contraceptive care.

News.title: Man guilty of murdering two men found in woods
News.content:
Desborough stood to listen to the verdicts with his hands behind his back.

He was wearing a grey T-shirt and glasses, and maintained a neutral expression while listening.

He was told he should "be alive" to the prospect of a whole life sentence when he is sentenced by Mr Justice Pushpinder Saini on Wednesday.

Witness impact statements would also be read out at the hearing, the court was told.

After the verdict, Coleman's family said in a statement: "We as a family would like to thank the police, prosecution and everyone involved in getting justice for Dan.

"Dan was a loving, caring and compassionate man who will be forever loved and sadly missed."

Aquilino's family said: "We are completely and utterly mortified in the violent murder of Claudio and the manner in which his body was disposed.

"Claudio will always be in our thoughts and we now pray he is at peace."

They said they had faced a "profoundly sad ordeal".

Det Supt Rachael Bentley, of Devon and Cornwall Police's major crime investigation team, described the killings as "callous and cold-blooded", as "both men were vulnerable and trusted James Desborough as their friend" before he brutally murdered them and "savagely desecrated their bodies".

She paid tribute to the victims' families, saying they "conducted themselves with a quiet dignity throughout this investigation and who have had to listen to, and see, some harrowing evidence".

Desborough was previously found guilty of strangling his 65-year-old cellmate Steven Kempster in September 2025, while on remand awaiting trial over the deaths of Coleman and Aquilino.

That trial had heard Kempster's snoring had annoyed Desborough.

Bentley said Desborough's taking of Kempster's "in this way was cowardly".

Helen Phillips of the Crown Prosecution Service said after the hearing that it had been a "large and extremely complex case".

"We worked closely with police from the very start of their investigation in Paramoor Woods, and then later with a second police team on the investigation into the murder at HMP Exeter, which ran in parallel," she said.

"The families of Claudio and Daniel have been so dignified throughout the investigation and trial process, even when faced in court with awful descriptions of what happened to their loved ones, and Desborough's attempts to blame Daniel for somehow being involved in the disposal of Claudio's body.

"As Desborough faces justice for his actions, my thoughts remain with the families and friends of his three victims."

Follow BBC Cornwall on X, external, Facebook, external and Instagram, external. Send your story ideas to spotlight@bbc.co.uk, external.

News.title: Chairman stole £22k from junior football club to fund cocaine habit
News.content:
A former junior football club chairman stole Â£22,491 from accounts and faked HMRC documents to feed his cocaine habit.

Karl Morecroft, 45, lied to club members at RTB Ebbw Vale while taking home the payments over the course of 15 months.

The club in Blaenau Gwent supported 330 children and relied on the goodwill of fundraisers, parents and volunteers to raise the money to keep going after the fraud.

Morecroft was given a 20-month jail term suspended for two years at Cardiff Crown Court on Monday, and must complete 180 hours of unpaid work and 50 rehabilitation days.

He was also ordered to pay Â£21,259 within three years and a default order of 12 months in prison if he failed to do so was imposed.

All American Airlines flights were temporarily grounded Tuesday after a nationwide IT outage.

“A technology issue briefly impacted connectivity for some of our systems on Tuesday evening,” American Airlines wrote on X. “Systems are coming back online now and flights are departing again.”

The major US carrier said it had put a temporary ground stop on its planes “while our teams worked to resolve the issue.”

The Air Traffic Control System Command Center wrote in a message at around 6:30 p.m. ET Tuesday that an IT outage was affecting all airports.

“We apologize to our customers for the inconvenience,” American Airlines added in its statement.

open image in gallery All American Airlines flights were temporarily grounded Tuesday after a nationwide IT outage ( AFP via Getty Images )

There were more than 1,500 reports of issues with American Airlines’ systems at around 6:30 ET, according to Downdetector.

Fifty-two percent of users reported issues with the carrier’s app.

“They can’t finish boarding my flight because the internet is down,” one traveler wrote on Downdetector at the time.

Another who identified as an American Airlines employee said the “whole system is down” and warned of delays.

open image in gallery The major US carrier said it put a temporary ground stop on its planes ‘while our teams worked to resolve the issue’ ( Getty Images )

There were more than 1,200 flight delays from American Airlines by Tuesday night, according to FlightAware.

So far, the number of disruptions has not been out of the norm. Wednesday saw nearly 1,300 American Airlines flight delays.

The Independent has reached out to American Airlines and the Federal Aviation Administration for comment.

None of the other major U.S. carriers — United Airlines, Delta Air Lines or Southwest Airlines — have reported issues with their flights.

In March, all JetBlue flights were temporarily grounded due to a “system outage,” the New York City-based carrier said at the time.

Andy Burnham has challenged his opponents to join him in putting aside political point-scoring to find a solution to England’s social care crisis.

The new Labour prime minister is set to hold a summit in Downing Street on Wednesday with Tory leader Kemi Badenoch and Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey to begin the process of thrashing out a way to deliver social care before it collapses the NHS.

Ahead of a speech he is set to deliver at a care home in north London on Wednesday morning, Mr Burnham said: “Last week I said we needed a different kind of politics: problem-solving, not point-scoring. Nowhere is that more urgent than social care.

“For decades, governments have kicked this issue down the road because they’ve seen it as too risky, too difficult, and too complicated.

“Politicians might have different views but I’m serious about fixing this issue and to do that, we have to find common ground and listen to others to find a way forward.

open image in gallery Andy Burnham has appealed to opposition leaders to help him find a solution ( Reuters )

“It’s time to draw a line under people playing politics when the human cost of that means carers struggling, families paying the price and our NHS buckling under the strain.”

However, the initiative comes amid growing concerns about the state of the economy and the government’s ability to pay for Mr Burnham’s initiatives.

Already there are major questions about how he will fund £2bn of commitments on removing VAT of energy bills, capping bus fares at £2 and reducing business rates of pubs and clubs by 20 per cent.

Added to that, a major think tank is set to warn that inflation will hit almost 4 per cent next year and the government’s capacity to borrow has maxed out meaning everything will need to be funded through tax rises and spending cuts.

This will hit defence in particular, where Mr Burnham will need to find between £5bn and £18bn to meet the UK’s commitments and it has been suggested wants to issue war bonds, another form of borrowing to fund the gap.

Ahead of the summit on Wednesday Sir Ed, who has ensured that the Lib Dems have prioritised demanding solutions to the care crisis, has said his party is willing to work with Mr Burnham. Ms Badenoch has also offered to work with Mr Burnham, but warned she will not support new tax rises to fund it.

open image in gallery Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch will not support tax rises ( PA Wire )

In 2009, when Mr Burnham was health secretary, he tried to find a common solution on care with a levy on assets when people died. But the Tories turned against him and accused him of trying to create a “death tax”.

Mr Burnham has not invited Reform UK to take part in the talks, even though they had been leading the polls for 15 months until Labour passed them this week.

However, Reform launched a preemptive attack, accusing Mr Burnham of wanting to revive his “death tax” plan, a claim that was immediately denied by Downing Street.

In a bid, though, to reach across the political divide, Mr Burnham said: “This comes down to a choice. We can carry on passing the problem to the next generation, or we can face it head on and work together to build a care system that gives people dignity, security and the support they deserve.

“This is about bringing back hope that we can finally fix the difficult issues that have been ignored for too long, and making Britain believe again.

“That's why I’m making this choice and I'm prepared to put everything I've got behind it.”

Visiting a care home on Wednesday, the prime minister will say he is making the choice to fix the broken social care system by finding common ground across party lines to tackle the big issues.

open image in gallery Nigel Farage and Reform have not been invited to the summit ( Reuters )

He will attempt to draw a line under decades of decline and a refusal to tackle these problems head-on, calling on all political parties to focus on solving problems and finding solutions together.

He will reiterate the need for a new kind of politics that puts differences aside in order to come together and face up to the challenges that Westminster has left unaddressed for too long.

He will be joined by the new health secretary Yvette Cooper and Baroness Louise Casey, who is leading the Independent Commission on Adult Social Care, which will draw up recommendations to deliver a National Care Service.

Baroness Casey will also launch the Big Conversation on Care, which will give the public their chance to share their views and help shape the future of adult social care in England so that it is designed for the people it is there to serve.

It will be open to everyone through a new online platform, starting off the conversation by asking people about the values and principles we should all expect from a care system.

Baroness Casey said: “For too long, we have been stuck in the same cycle: crisis, promises of reform, another review, and then retreat, while the people who need care, and their families, bear the brunt.

“Fixing adult social care is about far more than money. People are already paying for failure through council tax, pressure on the NHS, their savings, giving up work, and the forced sale of their homes. The choice is whether we keep putting money into a system that is unfair, unpredictable and broken, or have an honest conversation about how to build something better.

“That is why we need a public conversation on care that tackles the tough questions. It’s only by facing up to this problem together that we can fix social care once and for all.”

Responding, Tory shadow health secretary Stuart Andrew said: “Andy Burnham and Labour cannot rely on vague promises of reform without a clear plan for implementation and detail on what will happen when.

“The Conservatives are ready to work with Labour on measures that improve social care provided they are not reliant on yet more tax rises and borrowing.”

Sir Ed said: “There have been 22 failed attempts at reforming social care since 1997. To see the 23rd effort work, we need to do things differently.

"My party has been pushing for cross-party talks on care for years, because it is the only way to build a solution that actually works. For carers and for our country, nothing matters more, so I look forward to meeting the prime minister to begin these talks.”
