World.title: BP brings Turkey’s TPAO into Iraq’s Kirkuk project as Baghdad targets 1 million bpd exports
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — BP has agreed to sell a 15% stake in its Kirkuk operating business to Turkey’s state-owned oil firm TPAO, strengthening Ankara’s position in one of Iraq’s major oil reconstruction projects.

Baghdad and Turkey have also agreed to work together to increase Iraqi crude exports to 1 million barrels per day.

The agreement, announced during Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s visit to Ankara, comes after BP sold a 42% stake in BP Energy Company of Kirkuk Limited (BP ECKL) to U.S. oil producer ConocoPhillips earlier this month, leaving BP with a 43% operating interest, ConocoPhillips with 42%, and TPAO with the remaining 15%.

The restructured collaboration puts three big international energy corporations in charge of redeveloping Iraq’s Kirkuk oil complex, one of the country’s oldest and most crucial producing areas.

BP ECKL is responsible for developing the Kirkuk Development and Production Contract, which includes over 3 billion barrels of oil equivalent from the Baba and Avanah domes of the Kirkuk field, as well as the adjacent Bai Hassan, Jambur, and Khabbaz fields operated by Iraq’s state-owned North Oil Company.

The commercial agreement coincided with broader talks between Al-Zaidi and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who stated that the two countries intend to increase Iraqi oil exports to Turkey to 1 million barrels per day and sign a comprehensive energy cooperation agreement following the expiration of the decades-old Iraq-Turkey pipeline agreement.

Iraq’s Kirkuk reconstruction is anticipated to restore production from aging northern oilfields while increasing export capacity via Turkey.

After years of outages, Baghdad is working to restore northern crude shipments and expand export channels beyond the Gulf.

The investment also signals Turkey’s comeback as a commercial player in Kirkuk’s oil business almost a century after the Ankara Treaty of 1926, which saw Ankara give up territorial claims over the old Mosul vilayet in exchange for a temporary share of Iraqi oil royalties.

Unlike that approach, TPAO’s engagement is based on a commercial venture with BP and ConocoPhillips rather than a sovereign revenue-sharing agreement.

Al-Zaidi’s visit to Turkey, his fourth official foreign trip since taking office after stops in Washington, Doha, and Tehran, emphasized Baghdad’s strategy of combining foreign investment in its energy sector with broader plans to transform Iraq into a regional hub for energy exports, trade, and transportation through projects such as the Development Road corridor.

World.title: Iraq, Turkey deepen security, energy ties after PM’s Ankara visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq and Turkey agreed to deepen cooperation on security, energy, commerce, and the centerpiece Development Road project on Tuesday as Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi wrapped up his first official visit to Ankara since taking office.

Following conversations with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the two sides agreed to speed up the development of the Development Road corridor, which connects Iraq’s Grand Faw Port to Turkey and then to Europe, while also working to finalize a comprehensive bilateral energy cooperation deal.

In a joint statement, Baghdad and Ankara stated that they would strengthen cooperation in water resources, energy, trade, agriculture, transportation, investment, defense industries, and education, describing the Development Road as a critical project for increasing regional connectivity, economic integration, and long-term stability.

The two nations also reiterated their commitment to strengthening security cooperation in the face of transnational threats.

Erdogan commended Iraq’s support for Turkey’s war against extremist organizations, and both sides agreed to strengthen information sharing and security cooperation to defend their borders and maintain regional peace.

The visit comes as Iraq wants to improve economic ties with neighboring nations while portraying itself as a regional transportation and logistics center, linking the Gulf to Europe via new road, rail, and energy infrastructure.

Al-Zaidi’s travel comes after recent trips to the United States and Iran, where Iraq inked investment, transportation, and energy deals as part of a larger diplomatic effort to attract international investment and diversify the economy beyond oil.

The two countries also agreed to improve the legal framework regulating bilateral ties by ratifying outstanding agreements, signing new cooperation instruments, and holding the fifth meeting of the Iraq-Turkey High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council in Baghdad at a later date.

On regional concerns, Baghdad and Ankara said they would continue to closely coordinate on Middle Eastern events, confirming Syria’s unity and territorial integrity and pushing for increased regional stability.

Both parties underlined their support for the Palestinian cause.

The countries also agreed to celebrate the centenary of diplomatic relations next year with reciprocal visits and commemorative events, highlighting what both governments described as a strategic partnership that has expanded beyond security cooperation to include trade, energy, infrastructure, and regional connectivity.

World.title: Iraq PM publicly orders Transport Minister to sign Turkey corridor deal
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi publicly ordered his Transport Minister to sign a major agreement on the Development Road project at a joint ceremony with Turkish President Tayyip Erdoğan on Tuesday after an unexpected delay that temporarily interrupted the signing event.

The event occurred at a live broadcast ceremony in Ankara after the conclusion of discussions between Iraq and Turkey to strengthen cooperation in transportation, energy, and commerce.

Footage from the occasion shows Al-Zaidi interrogating Transport Minister Wahab al-Hasani about why the deal had not been signed before telling him to do it immediately.

Al-Zaidi then went to an interpreter, requesting that Erdogan be notified that he had instructed the Minister to sign.

The unexpected conversation temporarily overshadowed a tour meant to highlight progress on the Development Road project, a hallmark Iraqi program that would connect the Gulf’s Grand Faw Port to Turkey by a network of trains and roadways, establishing a significant commerce corridor between Asia and Europe.

Neither the Iraqi government nor Iraq’s Transport Ministry immediately stated the cause of the delay.

However, Iraqi politicians and media analysts said that al-Husseini originally delayed signing due to opposition from political groupings connected with the Iran-backed Badr Organization, led by Hadi al-Amiri, to whom the minister is affiliated.

According to the sources, opponents worried the corridor would reduce Iran’s position as a regional transit route.

The incident occurs at a crucial moment for Al-Zaidi, who has worked to establish Iraq as a regional transportation and logistics center while luring billions of dollars in international investment.

In recent weeks, the young Prime Minister has achieved a number of investment deals during travels to the United States, where American corporations have declared more than $60 billion in planned projects, and Iran, where Baghdad has inked transport and railway collaboration agreements.

He is also scheduled to visit Saudi Arabia later this week.

The Development Road initiative is fundamental to Iraq’s economic policy, with the goal of diversifying state income away from oil, increasing trade flows, and establishing Iraq as a major gateway linking the Gulf to Turkey and European markets.

The public dispute underscored Al-Zaidi’s political concerns as he strives to promote big economic changes while balancing opposing interests among Iraq’s strong political factions and armed organizations, some of whom have close links to Iran.

Analysts argue that managing those opposing interests remains one of his premiership’s most difficult challenges, as Baghdad seeks greater economic links with the United States, Turkey, and Gulf Arab governments while preserving relations with Tehran.

World.title: Saudi Arabia blames Iran-backed militias in Iraq for drone attack
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Saudi Arabia claimed on Tuesday that its air defenses intercepted and destroyed multiple drones targeting oil installations in the kingdom’s Eastern Province, accusing Iran-backed militants operating from Iraq of carrying out the assault.

Major General Turki al-Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi Defense Ministry, claimed the drones were intercepted many hours before reaching their objectives. He said that there were no immediate reports of damage or injuries.

Al-Maliki said that the drones were fired from Iraqi land by Iran-backed militias and that the strike was a terrorist act, adding that Saudi Arabia has the right to reply “at the appropriate time and place.”

There was no immediate claim of responsibility, and Iraqi officials had not independently verified Saudi Arabia’s claims.

The incident is the second occasion in recent days that Saudi Arabia has accused armed groups operating in Iraq of firing drones against the country.

Earlier, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi directed security agencies to investigate Saudi allegations that drones targeting the kingdom were launched from Iraqi territory, stating that Baghdad would prosecute anyone found responsible and emphasizing that Iraq would not allow its territory to be used to attack neighboring countries.

The latest accusation comes just days before Al-Zaidi is scheduled to visit Saudi Arabia for talks with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, where the two sides are expected to discuss expanding investment, trade, and regional cooperation following the prime minister’s recent trips to Washington, Tehran, and Ankara.

The recurring instances highlight one of the most difficult difficulties for Al-Zaidi’s administration as it strives to develop relations with Gulf Arab governments while exerting state control over Iran-aligned armed organizations that have carried out assaults independent of the Iraqi government.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit 526,000 bpd in May and June
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s average oil exports in May and June 2026 were roughly 526,470 barrels per day, compared to about 329,500 barrels per day in April, amid ongoing shipping and energy disruptions in the Gulf region.

The revenues generated from Iraqi oil exports saw an improvement over the last two months, supported by a relative increase in shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz and the activation of alternative export routes.

Oil prices fluctuated, remaining high at around $100 per barrel during May before falling below that level in June.

The rising oil prices boosted Iraq’s export income in May and June 2026, when there were fears about supply constraints and increased Asian demand, notably from China and India.

Iraqi oil exports have been under growing strain since the beginning of March, following the suspension of loading operations at southern ports due to the US war against Iran, which had a direct impact on marine security in the Strait of Hormuz.

According to the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO), Iraq’s total oil exports in May and June 2026 were roughly 32.11 million barrels, with a monthly average of over 16 million barrels.

The country’s oil exports reached 9.88 million barrels in April and around 18.6 million barrels in March.

Iraqi oil export earnings in May and June 2026 reached approximately $2.33 billion, averaging $1.16 billion per month, compared to $1.87 billion in April, $1.95 billion in March, and approximately $6.81 billion in February.

Experts believe that the current price levels of oil are likely to provide Baghdad with a better financial margin to mitigate some losses incurred from the significant decline in exports, even amidst ongoing security tensions in the region.

World.title: Iraqi PM arrives in Turkey on an official visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi arrived in the Turkish capital, Ankara, on Tuesday, for an official visit following an invitation from President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

Al-Zaidi said in a statement on X that his trip to Turkey will focus on investments, water, and development projects, as well as efforts to enhance stability in the region.

Turkish media highlighted the significance of the visit, as it is expected to broaden constructive collaboration between the two countries, particularly in the areas of water, energy, security, and economic cooperation, according to the state-run news agency (INA).

In addition to trade, security cooperation, and combating terrorism, al-Zaidi will discuss establishing a cooperative water management entity based on shared interests, as well as scientific collaboration and investment in advanced technology, to serve the interests of both Iraq and Turkey.

Al-Zaidi is scheduled to fly to Saudi Arabia on Thursday for an official visit, following his diplomatic trip to the Turkish capital, Ankara.

The trip is part of a larger regional diplomatic tour aiming to maintain regional balance and strengthen Iraq’s business connections.

The prime minister recently conducted high-level diplomatic visits to the United States on July 13 and Iran on July 23.

World.title: Ukraine rejects Iraqi official’s claims of Ukrainian cell operating in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Ukraine’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Tuesday dismissed statements by Iraq’s National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi, who claimed that Iraqi authorities had arrested a Ukrainian-linked cell responsible for carrying out attacks inside the country.

In an official statement, the ministry said the allegations were “groundless” and noted that no evidence had been presented to support the claims. It also pointed out that Al-Aboudi himself acknowledged during a televised interview that investigations into the matter were still ongoing.

According to the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry, Iraqi authorities did not communicate any information or concerns through diplomatic channels before the allegations were made publicly.

The ministry said that if Iraqi officials possessed credible evidence, the issue should have been raised through official diplomatic mechanisms rather than announced during a television interview. Instead, Kyiv said it first learned of the accusations through media reports.

Furthermore, Ukraine described the public remarks by a senior Iraqi official as “unacceptable and irresponsible” in the absence of supporting evidence. The ministry stressed that such statements contradict the principles of mutual respect between friendly nations and risk undermining relations between Iraq and Ukraine.

At the same time, Kyiv reaffirmed that it considers Iraq an important partner in the Middle East and remains committed to strengthening political, economic, and humanitarian cooperation between the two countries.

The Foreign Ministry also argued that the allegations mirror Russian propaganda narratives aimed at damaging Ukraine’s international reputation and weakening its partnerships across the Middle East.

Additionally, the statement suggested that the incident could have resulted from external information influence or formed part of a coordinated information campaign intended to disrupt Iraqi-Ukrainian relations.

Ukraine called on Iraqi authorities to address what it described as unfounded allegations and to prevent state institutions from promoting misinformation that could serve the interests of third parties.

The Ukrainian response follows remarks made on Monday by National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi during an interview on Dijlah TV. Al-Aboudi said Iraqi intelligence had identified what he described as Ukrainian interference inside Iraq and claimed security forces had arrested several individuals who allegedly carried out attacks on Iraqi territory.

He further stated that those detained confessed during questioning to working on behalf of Ukraine. However, Al-Aboudi did not identify the facilities allegedly targeted or specify whether the alleged operations extended beyond Iraq’s borders.

He also acknowledged that investigations into attacks carried out inside Iraq remain complex and require further examination before responsibility can be definitively assigned.

World.title: Iraqi PM expands powers as political deadlock delays cabinet completion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A dispute over Iraq’s remaining vacant cabinet positions has expanded beyond the selection of ministers, with political factions now focusing on the growing authority of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, according to a report published by Al-Mada newspaper.

The debate follows the leak of an official document indicating that Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi has reactivated and expanded the powers of the Commander-in-Chief Office, placing several key security institutions under its supervision while the Ministries of Interior and Defense remain without permanent ministers.

According to Al-Mada, several political sources believe the expanded office significantly increases the prime minister’s direct oversight of Iraq’s security apparatus.

The report says the office now oversees the Ministries of Interior and Defense, the Counter-Terrorism Service, the National Intelligence Service, the National Security Service, the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), border crossings, military industries, and other security-related institutions.

Consequently, some political figures have described the move as a “quiet coup” against Iraq’s post-2003 political framework, arguing that it centralizes authority within the prime minister’s office while reducing the practical influence of future ministers.

Meanwhile, Iraq’s cabinet remains incomplete, with only 14 ministries currently filled while nine ministerial portfolios remain vacant. According to the report, political negotiations have become increasingly complicated, as disagreements now extend beyond candidate names to broader questions of political influence and institutional control.

Sources cited by Al-Mada said the State of Law Coalition has proposed rotating senior security positions as part of efforts to break the deadlock, particularly regarding the Interior Ministry, which traditionally falls under the Shiite political share, while the Defense Ministry is typically allocated to Sunni representatives.

However, negotiations have yet to produce a breakthrough.

At the same time, Al-Mada reported that U.S. objections have become one of the main obstacles preventing completion of the cabinet. Political sources quoted in the report claim Washington opposes appointing individuals affiliated with armed factions to ministerial positions or senior executive offices.

The report says these objections have complicated negotiations among members of the Coordination Framework, with some factions insisting that if their nominees are rejected, similar restrictions should apply to other political parties. As a result, discussions over the remaining cabinet positions have largely stalled.

Political analysts interviewed by Al-Mada argue that the continued delay in appointing ministers has allowed Prime Minister Al-Zaidi greater flexibility in managing state institutions through acting officials and appointments within his office.

According to the report, some political parties fear that prolonging the vacancies could further strengthen the prime minister’s influence over Iraq’s security establishment, making future ministerial appointments less significant.

The report also notes that recent anti-corruption campaigns and shifting political alliances have altered the balance of power within the Coordination Framework, adding another layer of complexity to negotiations.

Supporters of the government, however, argue that the current arrangements are necessary to maintain continuity while negotiations continue.

Officials quoted by Al-Mada said acting appointments and the reactivation of the Commander-in-Chief Office ensure that security institutions continue functioning despite the absence of permanent ministers.

They also expressed confidence that political forces will eventually reach an agreement to complete the cabinet, stressing that Iraq faces significant challenges, including anti-corruption efforts, security reforms, weapons control, and economic pressures linked to oil exports.

Nevertheless, the report suggests that political parties continue to use the vacant ministries as leverage in negotiations with the prime minister, making the timeline for completing the government uncertain.

World.title: Centre may table bill to make deepfakes, digital arrest separate offences
World.content:
Digital arrest (representative image)

NEW DELHI: Government on Tuesday said it may introduce a bill in the ongoing session of Parliament making digital arrest and AI-generated deepfakes a distinct offence, after Supreme Court pointed out that existing penal laws do not define these offences.Solicitor General (SG) Tushar Mehta said the law will be aimed at categorising digital arrest and AI-generated deepfakes as specific offences with consequential punishments.During suo motu proceedings on the mechanism to curb the menace of digital arrest, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said SC has taken a harsh stand against those involved in digital arrest scams and denied them bail, but asked do penal laws define such offences?âYou (govt) may need to formally define the case of digital arrest in penal laws,â the bench told attorney general R Venkataramani.âIt (digital arrest) has elements of extortion, robbery and organised crime. Do you need to define this as a standalone offence with stringent consequences like freezing of assets of accused persons?â the bench asked attorney general R Venkataramani, who has been coordinating with a high-level inter-departmental committee constituted especially for dealing with the menace of digital arrest.Justice Bagchi said coming up with a law designed to deal with digital scams is a job that govt alone can do.âWe now have deepfakes which can be used for misleading people or can be used for cheating and impersonation. Using our (exclusive) powers under Article 142 of the Constitution, we can neither define a crime nor create a new offence,â he said.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told the bench that he has been consulted on this issue by govt and it is likely to introduce a relevant bill in the present session of Parliament. Venkataramani said because of a coordinated action facilitated by the inter-departmental committee, incidents of digital arrest have recorded a drastic fall. He said the panel is in the process of finalising a comprehensive report to identify gaps in the system and measures to plug them.Supreme Court after taking suo motu cognizance of spiralling incidents of digital arrest, especially targeting retired people and robbing them of their lifeâs savings, had tasked CBI to probe incidents being reported from across the country.Appearing for WhatsApp, senior advocate Kapil Sibal told SC that the social media platform is coordinating with govt to stop misuse of the platform for commission of crime.

World.title: MBBS admissions: NMC puts focus on ability, not disability
World.content:
NMC asks medical colleges to set up support units for students

NEW DELHI: Students with benchmark disabilities seeking admission to MBBS courses will now undergo an individual assessment of their functional abilities to determine whether they can acquire essential competencies required for the course with reasonable accommodation. National Medical Commission (NMC) Monday issued new guidelines requiring medical boards to evaluate each candidate's functional ability rather than relying solely on the type or extent of disability.Under the new framework, NMC-regulated medical college will now also have to set up an "enabling unit" for students with benchmark disabilities, providing a single point of contact for reasonable accommodation, academic and clinical support, and a barrier-free learning environment.Designated medical assessment boards will carry out an individual assessment of every candidate. The guidelines state that applicants cannot be declared ineligible solely on the basis of their diagnosis or the percentage of benchmark disability. Instead, boards must assess a candidate's functional abilities, the essential competencies required under competency-based medical education (CBME) curriculum, and whether reasonable accommodation can enable them to complete the course."After Supreme Court's constant follow-up and directions, NMC has amended its interim guidelines and issued revised guidelines for MBBS admissions of students with disabilities. The biggest change is the shift from assessing eligibility on the basis of the percentage of disability to evaluating functional competency. Clinical accommodations are reasonable modifications that enable medical students with benchmark disability to participate in clinical training and patient care without compromising academic standards or patient safety," said Prof Satendra Singh, coordinator at UCMS and GTB Hospital's enabling unit.The guidelines also require medical boards to consider assistive devices, adaptive technology, communication support and other reasonable accommodations before arriving at a decision.While emphasising inclusion, NMC has said patient safety will remain an important consideration.On enabling units, NMC directed these should be set up in compliance with Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, and recent Supreme Court directions aimed at ensuring inclusive medical education.The unit will also receive and address requests for disability-specific accommodations during the course of study, including clinical training and internship, according to the circular.

World.title: UK company in spotlight as Nishikant Dubey vows 'disclosure' in Parliament
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey Tuesday said he will soon make a disclosure in Parliament about a UK-registered company allegedly linked to an Indian MP, igniting speculation over who could be the target.

"Which Indian politician is a director in Backops Limited (UK)? Which companies have their address at 2 Frognal Way, London NW3 6XE? What is the connection of that Indian neta with Brian Lovegrove and Ulrik McKnight? Everything will be revealed inside Parliament," Dubey posted on X, piquing interest and sparking buzz hinting that Parliament might witness yet another showdown.

Talking to reporters in Parliament complex, the Godda MP elaborated on his claim by saying that two individuals, Brian Lovegrove and Ulrik McKnight, linked to Backops Limited, were associated with hundreds of companies, including a few TV channels, all registered at the same address: a claim that implied that Backops Limited was not a genuine business enterprise.

The BJP MP said that the MP in question had registered Backops Limited in the UK in 2003.

"I intend to raise all these matters in Parliament: Who is this MP, and how did they register this company? What is their relationship with Lovegrove and McKnight, and what role does '2 Frognal Way' play in the 'tukde-tukde gang'?" Dubey said.

World.title: NEET row: CBI chargesheets 13 in paper leak
World.content:
File photo: NEET-UG 2026 leak probe

3 NTA subject experts and several middlemen among those named

NEW DELHI: Seventy-seven days after it filed an FIR and began a probe into the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case, CBI Tuesday filed a chargesheet against 13 individuals arrested in the case. These include three NTA subject experts, in chemistry, biology and physics. Several middlemen who sourced and distributed these leaked questions have also been charged.The agency has cited 360 witnesses, 422 documents and 43 material objects to back its case, which concluded that persons responsible for setting the questions had leaked them, in connivance with their associates, including middlemen and coaching centre owners.The accused have been charged with offences of criminal conspiracy, cheating, criminal breach of trust, destruction of evidence and others under BNS, for the offence of criminal misconduct under Prevention of Corruption Act and for offences under Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024."Digital forensic analysis reports, handwriting expert opinions and academic experts' opinions regarding leaked questions were obtained.These reports confirmed the role of the accused in the circulation of leaked questions prior to the date of examination," CBI said in its final report. All 13 accused persons are in judicial custody. If the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill is passed, their trial is expected to be completed within three months. CBI had started an investigation on a complaint of the department of higher education on May 1, detailing irregularities and allegations of a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination."The probe team led by agency chief Praveen Sood acted swiftly to unearth the source of the leak within weeks of registration of the case. The channel from source of the leak to the beneficiary candidates was unearthed, leading to the identification of the chain," an officer said.After the filing of an FIR, Sood immediately formed multiple teams comprising 72 officers and personnel along with eight cyber forensic experts. "Searches were conducted at 92 locations in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Haryana, Delhi and other states. These searches led to seizure of incriminating material like digital and communication devices, documents, etc," a CBI officer said.Forensic imaging and analysis of the incriminating material was undertaken. Intelligence agencies also gave crucial technical inputs. The first arrest in this case was made on May 13, within 24 hours of registration of the case. A dozen others were subsequently arrested from Pune and other places.The accused, arrested and now chargesheeted, include NTA subject experts Manisha Mandhare (biology), Pralhad Vithalrao Kulkarni (chemistry) and Manisha Sanjay Havaldar (physics), along with middlepersons and intermediaries Manisha Sanjay Waghmare, Dhananjay Nivrutti Lokhande, Shubham Madhukar Khairnar, Yash Yadav, Mangilal Biwal, Vikash Biwal, Dinesh Biwal and Dr Manoj Bhagwanrao Shirure.The chargesheet also names prominent coaching institute figures Shivraj Raghunath Motegoankar, owner of RCC Coaching Institute in Latur, and Tejas Harshadkumar Shah, physics faculty member and COO at APMA Coaching Institute in Pune.The money trail analysis has been conducted and several bank accounts, bank lockers and a demat account of the accused have been frozen. "Further investigation and forensic analysis is continuing in the case. CBI is committed to ensuring that those responsible for such offences face full legal consequences for their actions," the spokesperson added.With pending forensic reports expected in the coming days, CBI is likely to file a supplementary chargesheet in the case, the sources said.

World.title: 1st direct freight train opens new India-Nepal chapter
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In a new chapter for India-Nepal rail connectivity, the first-ever direct commercial container freight train - carrying canola oil in 40 tank wagons - completed its journey from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar Customs Yard in Nepal last week.

In a statement, railway ministry said the new arrangement is expected to substantially reduce transit time, logistics costs and cargo handling, while improving efficiency, reliability and competitiveness of cross-border trade.

The achievement builds upon the broad-gauge rail link between Jogbani (India) and Biratnagar (Nepal) inaugurated in June 2023. "Following the signing of the revised Letter of Exchange (LoE) in Nov 2025, direct commercial rail movement to Biratnagar has now become operational, opening new opportunities for bilateral trade and economic cooperation," it said.

The direct freight service is expected to provide a significant boost to the movement of import and export cargo by offering a faster, more economical and environmentally sustainable mode of transportation. It reduces multiple handling points improving supply chain efficiency.

World.title: NEET protest: All SOPs followed, pellet gun use on protesters authorised, reveals CRPF review
World.content:
NEW DELHI: All standard operating procedures (SOPs) and anti-riot drills were followed during the July 20 police action against anti-NEET leak protesters, which included the authorised use of "non-lethal" means like pellet gun, a CRPF post-event analysis has said.

CRPF sources told TOI that upon carefully examining the response of its anti-riot unit, Rapid Action Force, it is evident that force gradient was followed, with pump action gun being used only after lower-grade measures like public announcements for crowd dispersal, tear gas and lathicharge failed to effectively control the mob. Around 3-5 protesters were injured by the metal pellets. Also, 47 RAF personnel were injured, with six sustaining head injuries.

When contacted, CRPF DG G P Singh said the matter was "sub judice" and any findings or view of the force on RAF action would be placed before Supreme Court. RAF sources said the use of force on July 20 was authorised by Delhi Police, in line with the SOPs and the law.

âPolice, RAF attacked with stones, iron railsâ

Sources claimed the mob had some motivated elements attacking personnel of Delhi Police and RAF with stones and, in some cases, even iron rails.

As per BNSS, an executive magistrate may order use of civil force to disperse an unlawful assembly after carefully assessing the situation.





In Delhi, this magisterial authority is vested with the Delhi Police commissioner, and delegated to junior commissioners till the level of the assistant commissioner of police. âRAF deployed at protest sites uses anti-riot gear only with authorisation; which in this case came from the DCP/ACP in charge of the protest site.

Such authorisation is in writing and as per a format used at all sites of unlawful assembly; no order is given verbally,â said an officer.

CRPF sources said pump action guns are an approved, ânon-lethalâ measure to control unlawful assemblies. âTheir use, with the force gradient being followed and under authorisation by the competent officer, is as per the SOP,â said an officer.

J&K high court had, in its 2016 ruling on a PIL challenging pellet use, said: âSo long as there is violence by unruly mobs, use of force is inevitable. What kind of force has to be used at the relevant point of time or in a given situation has to be decided by the persons in charge of the place where the attack is happening. This court in writ jurisdiction, without any finding rendered by the competent forum/authority cannot decide whether the use of force in a particular incident is excessive or not.

â

Supreme Court later dismissed the special leave petition against this order, stating, âThe use of pellet guns, if at all done by any agency, has not only not been barred, but validated through these orders.â

World.title: India is second-largest sailor supplier in world
World.content:
File photo: Ships in the sea

NEW DELHI: With a 12.2% share of global seafaring workforce, India has become the world's second-largest supplier of sailors, according to BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026. The Philippines continues to be the largest supplier of seafarers globally.The report published every five years is widely regarded by the global maritime industry as the most authoritative assessment of seafarer supply and demand. As per the report, share of Indian sailors has doubled in the past five years."BIMCO-ICS report is the most credible and every maritime nation follows this. India's strength is particularly evident in the officer cadre. We supply over 1.4 lakh officers, accounting for 13.4% of the world's officer workforce, while 1.7 lakh ratings represent 11.29% of the global ratings serving aboard merchant vessels," said an official.

World.title: Ahmedabad tragedy: Supreme Court accepts pilot dad's plea not to make Air India crash report public
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday accepted the request of the father of the pilot, who died in the Ahmedabad air crash last June, for not making public the final inquiry report, expected in Oct, and the Centre said that it will furnish the report in a sealed cover to the court.

Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that govt respects the sentiments of the pilot's father and will submit the final report, as soon as it is finalised, to Supreme Court in a sealed cover. The SG, however, brushed aside objections to the ongoing inquiry into the crash of Air India's London flight that killed 260, all but one passenger and many on ground.

Appearing for the NGO, advocate Prashant Bhushan attempted to punch holes in the inquiry, terming it to be biased because of absence of independent members in the probe team and said it did not follow the standard operating procedure for such inquiries. The solicitor general said the inquiry is being conducted following prescribed process scrupulously.

Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) on July 14 had responded to the petition filed by the deceased pilot's father Pushkar Raj Sabharwal, and said, "In view of the nature, scale and complexity of the present accident, the AAIB has carefully assessed the timeline for completion of the investigation.





In all probability, the investigation activities, subject to resolution of the pending external dependencies, are anticipated to be completed within six weeks.

"

"Thereafter, the draft final report, following completion of the analysis phase, is expected to be ready approximately in Oct 2026," it had said. "As per the treaty mandate, upon preparation of draft final report, the same has to be mandatorily shared with the Accredited Representatives of the State of Design and Manufacture, for comments, as required under the relevant rules of International Civil Aviation Organisation , which in the present case - the National Transportation Safety Board, USA.

"

World.title: Japan earthquake LIVE: At least two dead in shopping mall hit by quake, says report
World.content:
An earthquake registering a magnitude of 7.1 shook Kumamoto on Japan’s southern main island of Kyushu late Tuesday (July 28, 2026) afternoon, causing damage and injuries, officials said. A tsunami advisory was temporarily issued but was lifted within two hours, the Japan Meteorological Agency said.

Also read | Japan earthquake: ‘Considerable’ number of people reported dead in Kumamoto mall after earthquake

Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, in a message posted on X, said her government has set up a task force to gather information, assess possible damage and prepare for rescue operations if needed.

“Many people” were feared trapped in a stricken shopping mall, authorities said, after the quake toppled buildings, sparked fires and reportedly injured more than 100.

Ms. Takaichi later told reporters that there have been reports of a number of injuries and damages to roads, bridges and buildings, as well as blackouts and fire, though details are still unclear. Ms. Takaichi warned people cooking to be careful with fire and with shards of broken glass.

World.title: Ahead of 2027 Punjab polls, AAP’s welfare spree sparks questions over timing, intent
World.content:
As Punjab goes to Assembly polls in early 2027, the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) in the last few months has rolled out a set of welfare schemes, prompting questions about whether the timing reflects genuine intent or an election-driven strategy.

Even as the Opposition parties have targeted the AAP government over the timing of launching welfare schemes amid the run-up to the Punjab elections, the AAP asserted that AAP’s intent is to serve the people and, despite the financial mess created by the previous government, the AAP has fulfilled its pre-poll guarantees.

With barely a few months left for the Assembly election in Punjab, the State government on July 1 started its ‘Mukh Mantri Mawan Dhian Satikar Yojna’, under which women above 18 years of age from the general category will receive ₹1,000 every month, while those belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC) category will receive ₹1,500. This was one of the key pre-poll promises on which the AAP sought votes during its election campaign in the 2022 Assembly election. The Opposition parties have repeatedly criticised the ruling party for taking years to roll out the cash payout, terming the move an election-eve gimmick timed to win over voters before the next elections.

All India Congress Committee general secretary and Rajya Sabha MP Randeep Surjewala, talking to The Hindu on Tuesday (July 28, 2026), said that while voters in Punjab elected the AAP government on March 16, 2022 with high expectations of change but the government kept waiting for almost five years to “start this scheme”, and has now launched it just a few months before the election, which is nothing more than a mere “election trick”.

“Inclusive, participative development and making people partners in the State’s progress is intrinsic to our democracy. But what Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and his government are doing is a tool to befool, dupe and deceive gullible and simple Punjabis, including our sisters and mothers,” said Mr. Surjewala.

“The State is passing through a financial emergency. Punjab government needs ₹21,472 crore every year to implement the scheme. Does the State have the money to sustain the scheme? Or are such schemes merely for three months up till the elections as a vote-garnering exercise? If Mr. Mann and AAP were sincere in making the women of Punjab participants in governance, then why did he wait five years until the very end of his tenure to initiate the scheme?” quipped the Congress leader.

Asserting that the Punjab government was following the “deception model of the Bharatiya Janata Party government of Maharashtra”, he said, “Before the general elections in Maharashtra in November 2024, BJP announced the ‘Ladki Behen Yojana’ to give ₹1,500 every month, and after the elections, it deleted the names of 80 lakh women. BJP did the same in Haryana and later embroiled the scheme in technicalities. Your playbook of deception and trickery is the same.

Earlier, in January this year, the Punjab government also launched ‘Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojna’, extending free treatment of up to ₹10 lakh to every family. Also, the government started Meri Rasoi Yojna, which provides free quarterly kitchen kits to economically weaker families.

Meanwhile, Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Cheema said that AAP is the first government in the country to guarantee free healthcare, free education, free electricity and free bus travel for women.

“When we came to power, Punjab was in an economic morass and debt trap due to the previous faulty policies of successive governments of the Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal. We have improved the situation. Adequate financial arrangements have been made for the welfare schemes. We gave 300 units of free power and ‘Pind clinics’. The AAP government has provided ₹1 crore to the families of defence personnel who lost their lives in the line of duty. He further said that the State government provides a ₹2 crore honorarium to the families of police personnel in case of losing their lives during duty. All this shows our intent of serving the people of Punjab is absolutely clear,” he said.

“Punjab government reserved posts for the Scheduled Castes for the first time for the appointment of law officers. The Congress and Akalis never thought about the betterment of the marginalised; it’s only the AAP that is doing overall development in Punjab,” he added.

World.title: CPI(M), PDP condemn killings by security forces in POK
World.content:
The CPI(M) and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) expressed concern in Srinagar on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) about continued repression and killings by security forces in Pakistan Occupied Kashmir (POK) over the past 24 hours.

“I stand with the people of Pakistan‑administered Kashmir — their demands are just: end harsh economic policies, restore fair governance, and protect democratic rights. The deaths and injuries in Rawalakot, Muzaffarabad, and Kotli are a painful reminder that grievances met with force only deepen the crisis,” said CPI(M) leader and legislator M. Y. Tarigami.

Pointing to the Supreme Court of Pakistan’s ruling on the 12 refugee seats he added that “this struggle must be resolved constitutionally and peacefully — through dialogue, not repression”. “We express solidarity with families of the fallen. We call for accountability, relief for affected communities, and a political solution that honours rights and dignity,” Mr. Tarigami said

PDP leader and former minister Naeem Akhtar also appealed to Pakistan “to stop atrocities against our people in the part of our State that you hold”. “People’s demands cannot be brushed under the carpet by using brute violence. Engagement and dialogue are the only way forward to resolve all issues in the region.”

According to reports emerging from POK, 21 people were killed and dozens were injured after security forces opened fire on supporters of the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) — a civil society group pressing for local demands — in Rawalakot on Monday (July 27, 2026).

World.title: Delhi HC directs ECI to avoid imposing ‘unbearable’ burden on teachers during SIR
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday (July 27, 2026) directed the Election Commission of India (ECI) to ensure that schoolteachers deployed for the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls are not subjected to an “unbearable” burden.

A Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia reiterated that the poll body’s constitutional powers must be exercised in compliance with the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.

The Bench clarified that there was no dispute regarding the ECI’s power to engage teachers for election-related work. However, it emphasised that Section 27 of the RTE Act, which prohibits teachers from being assigned non-educational duties except for population census, disaster relief and election work, “cannot be lost sight of”.

ECI counsel stated that teachers being requisitioned for performing the work relating to revision of the electoral roll are being engaged only after school hours, holidays and non-teaching days.

“We, however, may also emphasise that after working in a school for 6-8 hours, a teacher engaged to perform election duties may cause stress and therefore it is expected of the ECI and its officers to be mindful of the stress which a teacher undergoes while performing election-related duties after the school hours and non-teaching days,” the bench observed.

“Accordingly, we direct that while assigning the work related to elections to the teachers... they shall take all appropriate steps so that the election-related work does not cause so much stress on teachers which may lead to unbearable burden,” the Bench said.

During the hearing, counsel for the petitioners disputed the Election Commission’s submission that teachers were being assigned SIR duties only after school hours, on holidays and on non-teaching days, describing the claim as “100 per cent lie.”

The Bench said, “You bring to the notice of the court that any of the teachers have been deployed during the course of the teaching hours, we will take action against them”.

The Bench also questioned the ECI over a circular issued on July 26 directing school principals not to initiate disciplinary action against teachers for unauthorised leave or absence. The Bench asked why such a direction was necessary if teachers were, as claimed by the Commission, being engaged only after school hours.

“Can any teacher be charged with misconduct of unauthorised leave if she is present during school hours? If they are engaged after school hours, where is the question of there being any absence or unauthorised leave?” the Court asked. It added that while it was not undermining the ECI’s electoral exercise, a balance had to be maintained with the mandate of the RTE Act. “It seems you are least bothered about the RTE Act... This whole letter is threatening,” the Bench remarked.

When the ECI submitted that teachers may spend about five hours after school performing Booth Level Officer (BLO) duties, the Court expressed concern over the cumulative workload saying the teacher should not be expected to work for nearly 11 hours a day, particularly as many of them are women with family responsibilities.

“We are not curtailing the rights of the ECI, but we are also conscious of the conditions of teachers... You have to humanise,” the Court observed.

The petition, filed by advocates Rajesh Kumar Gogna and Ashok Agarwal, contended that the mass deployment of government, municipal and government-aided school teachers for the SIR exercise was adversely affecting the education of lakhs of students in Delhi. It alleged that in several schools, regular teaching staff had been withdrawn during school hours, forcing classes to be handled by guest teachers or teachers from unrelated subjects.

The Court has posted the matter for further hearing on August 20.

World.title: CBI files charge sheet against 13 accused in NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case
World.content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has filed a charge sheet against 13 arrested accused persons in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case, the agency said on Tuesday (July 28, 2026). All of them are currently in judicial custody.

The charge sheet comes days after Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned from the post on July 25, in the wake of over a month-long agitation led by the Cockroach Janta Party.

The agency has invoked provisions related to criminal conspiracy, cheating, criminal breach of trust, destruction of evidence and other associated charges under the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act.

It has cited 360 witnesses, 422 documents, and 43 material objects in the charge sheet.

The agency registered the case based on a complaint lodged by the Department of Higher Education on May 12, alleging irregularities in the conduct of the NEET-UG 2026 examination, which was held on May 3. The test was subsequently cancelled.

The CBI formed multiple teams with 72 officials and personnel, along with eight cyber forensic experts, to investigate the case. Searches were carried out at 92 locations in Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, and other States.

“These searches led to the seizure of incriminating material like digital and communication devices, documents etc. Forensic imaging and analysis of the incriminating material has been undertaken,” said the agency, adding that source of the leak was unearthed within weeks.

“The path from source of the leak to the beneficiary candidates was unearthed, leading to the identification of the chain. The first arrest in this case was made on May 13, 2026, it said.

Among the arrested are three National Testing Agency (NTA) subject experts in chemistry (P.V. Kulkarni), biology (Manisha Gurunath Mandhare), and physics (Manisha Sanjay Havaldar).

Another key accused is Shivaraj Motegaonkar, a professor and owner of RCC Coaching Institute in Maharashtra’s Latur.

Several alleged intermediaries who sourced and distributed the leaked questions were also held. Tejas Harshadkumar Shah, physics faculty and chief operating officer at APMA Coaching Institute, Pune, was also arrested.

“Digital forensic analysis reports, handwriting expert opinions and academic experts’ opinions regarding leaked questions have been obtained. These reports confirmed the role of the accused in the circulation of leaked questions before the date of examination,” said the CBI. Further investigation is under way.

World.title: Unwise to link women’s quota with delimitation: K.T. Rama Rao
World.content:
Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) leader K.T. Rama Rao (KTR), said that the protests by students over the leak of the NEET exam paper was “unique” and an “inflexion” point in Indian polity and that the Delimitation Bill, if it is tabled in Parliament, should ensure that the southern States maintain their level of representation in the Lok Sabha.

Speaking to The Hindu during his visit to Delhi, Mr. Rao said that the protests were not just about paper leaks but seemed to be channelling a number of frustrations among the people that needed a trigger point. While anti-incumbency had built up, he said, he conceded that the BJP still had time to recover, but that the lessons for the Opposition were just as dire.

“What you effectively saw was the manifestation of a series of events and not just one isolated incident that resulted in this. They (the BJP) still have time to make amends and maybe win the youngsters back. Also the situation clearly shows that it was not the principle Opposition nor the Opposition block as such, that could inspire confidence, and it had to be a student led, kind of leaderless, rudderless kind of a moment, which just emanated like the Arab Spring had (in 2011). Therefore, it’s unique and it certainly is an inflection point in Indian politics. If you ask me, Prime Minister Modi and his government has never looked as vulnerable as they did in the last 15 days,” he said.

On delimitation Mr. Rao said that it was “unwise” to intertwine women reservation and delimitation the way the government had done in April in the special session to consider the two Bills.

“Women’s reservation can be implemented without linking it or without intertwining it with delimitation. So the fundamental point of Government of India trying to fire the delimitation gun, you know, using a women reservation as a shoulder to lean on is wrong, whereas the Women’s Reservation Act has already been passed by Parliament,” he said. “Government of India needs to realise that they’re sitting on a powder keg. If they mess with the current ratio, where the southern States as a block have 24% representation in Parliament, then most certainly there will be a serious protest erupting in the south,” he said.

He suggested his own formula for doing so. “Why is delimitation done in the first place? Because you want increased participation, representative democracy, more decentralisation, etc. So the one way to do it, is basically increase the number of MLA seats. If they can go ahead and increase the number of MLA seats across the country, there’s 4000 plus now. That can be enhanced to 6000. Nobody has a problem. Because then it’s within the geographical confines of one State and when it comes to Parliament, you’re not disturbing the status quo. The second formula could be one where you actually sit across a table, come to the consensus on how this 24% of South can be maintained as is, so that there is parity and balance,” he said.

“There should not be a penalty for good implementation of population policies, you can’t have a noose around our neck, say that this is good for you (southern States), and stifle our voice,” he said.

World.title: Paper leak Bill a milestone, says govt; Opposition calls it ‘cosmetic exercise’
World.content:
Treasury and Opposition benches sparred in the Lok Sabha on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) as the House took up the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, with the Opposition describing it as an “admission of failure”.

Also read | Bill proposing harsher punishment for paper leaks taken up for discussion; milestone legislation, says government

Initiating the debate for the Opposition, Congress deputy leader Gaurav Gogoi questioned why the government was amending a law it had hailed as “historic” just two years ago.

“If that law was so effective, why has the government been forced to bring such major amendments within two years?” Mr. Gogoi asked, calling the Bill a “cosmetic exercise” that reflected the failure of the 2024 law enacted after the earlier NEET-UG controversy.

He argued that the latest paper leak had exposed the government’s inability to protect the integrity of public examinations and said harsher punishments alone would not end the menace without structural reforms in the education system.

Referring to the nationwide student protests, Mr. Gogoi condemned the use of pellet guns and electric batons, saying students had taken to the streets out of “deep pain and anxiety” over their future.

The Congress leader also questioned the fate of recommendations by the 2024 committee headed by former ISRO chairman K. Radhakrishnan and sought details of the 47 officials the government claimed to have removed or transferred from the National Testing Agency (NTA).

“Who are these 47 people, when the sanctioned strength of the NTA is 34?” Mr. Gogoi asked. He also questioned why the government had so much faith in the NTA chairman. “Is it because he is associated with a particular Sangh?” he asked.

The Congress leader also alleged that 44 of the 45 accused in the 2024 NEET-UG paper leak case had secured bail.

Mr. Gogoi and several other MPs objected to BJP MP Dharmendra Pradhan being given a “grand welcome” by his party colleagues in Parliament even after he had to resign as the Union Education Minister. “It is as if he had won a war with Pakistan,” Mr. Gogoi said.

Samajwadi Party (SP) MP Dimple Yadav lashed out at the government for the police action against protesting students. “The government could pressurise some of the MPs sitting here to try and pass the Delimitation Bill, but it could not put pressure on students,” she said, while reading out the names of the students who allegedly died by suicide over the NEET paper leak.

BJP counters

Responding to the Opposition, BJP MP Anurag Thakur hit out at Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi for sitting on a dharna outside the Prime Minister’s residence, saying Mr. Gandhi did so because students did not ask him to lead the protests.

Mr. Thakur also said Prime Minister Narendra Modi continues to be popular among the country’s youth, adding his Instagram video on the issue had garnered over 400 million views.

Defending the Bill, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj accused the Opposition of “selective outrage”, contending that paper leaks had also occurred under the UPA government’s tenure. Calling the amendment “transformative”, she said it would strengthen the legal framework through faster prosecution, stricter punishment and measures to tackle organised examination mafias.

Shiv Sena MP Shrikanth Shinde accused the Opposition of politicising the issue while the Modi government is taking decisive steps to tackle examination paper leaks.

World.title: You were at Delhi protest, but your police booked protesters in Kerala: Pinarayi Vijayan to CM Satheesan
World.content:
Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan on Tuesday directed the state Home Department to examine the demand for the withdrawal of cases registered against those who took to the streets in solidarity with the recent students’ protests in Delhi’s Jantar Mantar.

Earlier in the day, Opposition Leader Pinarayi Vijayan wrote a letter to the Chief Minister, demanding that all cases registered in Kerala in this regard be withdrawn unconditionally.

The Chief Minister’s Office said the letter has been handed over to the Home Department for further action.

Police sources said the exact number of cases registered in Kerala in connection with the protests was not known. Most of the cases were registered as bailable offences for unlawful assembly or gathering at public places without permission.

World.title: 2022 Khargone communal violence: 11 accused acquitted by court as prosecution case collapses
World.content:
A Madhya Pradesh sessions court has acquitted 11 men accused in the 2022 Khargone Ram Navami violence after the prosecution’s case collapsed with eight of its 11 eyewitnesses failing to identify any of the accused and laboratory findings failing to establish the alleged use of petrol bombs or any explosive substance.

The case arose from the communal violence that erupted in Khargone on April 10, 2022 during Ram Navami processions.

According to the prosecution, mobs armed with stones, swords and petrol bombs attacked houses in the Bhatwadi locality between 6 pm and 9 pm, setting homes and motorcycles on fire, damaging property and allegedly trespassing into residences. One man, identified as Idris Khan, was killed in the violence.

Police charged 11 men — Ibadat, Sadiq, Abdullah, Saheb alias Shahib, Sheryar, Faizal, Azam, Shabbir, Imran, Mustaq and Rajik — with rioting, arson, house trespass and offences under the Explosive Substances Act in connection with the violence.

A day after the violence, the district administration had carried out a demolition drive, razing 16 houses and 29 shops in five localities of the town. The then Madhya Pradesh Home Minister, Narottam Mishra, had said “Jis ghar se patthar aaye hain, us ghar ko hi pattharon ka dher banayenge (Will turn the houses from where the stones were hurled to a heap of rubble).”



In a detailed judgment Monday, Fourth Additional Sessions Judge Mukesh Nath held that the prosecution’s case collapsed on the question of identification. The court found that eight of the 11 eyewitnesses examined by the prosecution completely failed to implicate the accused, no test identification parade was ever conducted, there was no explanation on how police selected the accused from a mob of about 50 people, and forensic evidence failed to establish the alleged use of petrol bombs.

The court recorded that eight prosecution witnesses, including complainants and victims, “did not support the prosecution story.”

“None of these eight witnesses identified any of the accused; none stated that any accused had committed any act constituting the incident; no substantive evidence emerged in their testimonies against any accused,” it said.



Even after they were declared hostile, “the prosecution derived no benefit, and no substantive fact implicating the accused persons came on record.” The court concluded that “the involvement of the accused persons in the offence is neither disclosed nor proved in any manner”.

The prosecution’s case rested substantially on a local resident, Vaishnavi Jain, whom the court described as the only witness to attribute the incident to all 11 accused. But the judgment found her evidence riddled with contradictions.

The court noted that Vaishnavi claimed she recognised all the accused by their faces, while her own father Dinesh Jain and brother Akash Jain both stated that the rioters had “their faces covered with cloth”.

Akash told the court he saw only four or five people and “does not know the persons who committed the incident… because he could not see their faces, as their faces were covered with cloth.” The court held that “no substantive fact against the accused persons emerges from the testimony of this witness, nor does his testimony establish the identity of the accused persons.”



The judgment was equally critical of Dinesh Jain’s testimony. Although he identified all 11 accused in court, the judge said that “merely because a witness identifies the accused persons does not establish their involvement in the offence unless the witness specifically states that the person identified was among those who committed the crime”.

The court found that Dinesh Jain admitted he had viewed the crowd from 500-600 metres away, had not seen the accused from the front, had no prior personal acquaintance with them, accepted that the rioters had covered their faces, and ultimately admitted that “he could not say who burnt the door of his house, who threw the stones, or who committed the looting”.

The judge found it “not natural, satisfactory, or reliable” that someone could identify people merely by seeing them “from behind at a distance of 500-600 metres”, particularly when the witness accepted that the rioters had covered their faces.



The court identified several investigative lapses that further weakened the prosecution. It noted that Vaishnavi’s name did not appear as an eyewitness in any of the written complaints or the FIR, despite both being lodged two days after the violence. It also found “no explanation for the delay of two days in lodging the First Information Report.”

The court observed that Vaishnavi’s police statement under Section 161 CrPC was recorded 51 days after the incident, with “no explanation” for the delay in recording the statement of what the prosecution claimed was its most important eyewitness.

The judgment questioned how police had implicated all 11 accused in the first place. It noted that the FIR named only six accused, while five others were added later without any explanation.



The prosecution also failed to establish its allegation that petrol bombs had been used. Referring to the State Forensic Science Laboratory report, the court recorded that “no residues of inflammable petroleum hydrocarbons (petrol/diesel/kerosene) were detected” in the seized bottle fragments and burnt material.

World.title: ‘PM must change angle of his heart, not of cameras’: Priyanka Gandhi slams action on protesters
World.content:
Participating in the debate on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha on Tuesday, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra launched a sharp attack on the Narendra Modi government over the police crackdown on student protesters in Delhi and other places, saying that the “Prime Minister will have to change the angle of his heart rather than that of the cameras” if he wants to win over the Gen Z.

Recalling her visit to a Delhi hospital to meet the mother of a girl who was critically injured in police action on protesting students and youths during their march on Parliament on July 20, Priyanka said she was “displeased” with VIP visits and asserted that she would fight alone for her daughter.



“I want to ask the Prime Minister and Home Minister what was the need to perpetrate such atrocities on a girl. What was the need to use pellet guns and AK-47 on students? Will the Home Minister answer who gave this order – the PM or the HM? The country is asking this today,” Priyanka said.

She took strong objection to BJP MPs garlanding Dharmendra Pradhan in the Parliament complex after his resignation as the Union education minister, saying they behaved as if a “superstar” had arrived. Earlier, her party colleague Gaurav Gogoi also took a swipe at the BJP, saying its MPs hailed Pradhan as if he had just won a war against Pakistan.

Pradhan was forced to resign on July 25 as the Modi government accepted the demands made by young protesters led by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), who held a sit-in at Jantar Mantar since June 20 in protest against the NEET-UG paper leaks, among other issues.



The Lok Sabha took up the amended anti-paper leaks Bill for consideration and passing, ending a week-long logjam in Parliament.

The Congress’s onslaught on the government came after Union minister Jitendra Singh, while presenting the Bill, pointed out that that it was an amendment to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, to make the law more stringent, which has been brought to protect the interest of students and youths.

Singh said that paper leaks have happened in many states under the governments of various parties and that the Modi government’s 2024 law was perhaps the first-ever in India to combat various exam malpractices.

The minister recalled past paper leaks in the Railway Recruitment Board exam in 2009, All India Engineering exam in 2011, and the AIIMS Delhi paper leak in 2012, saying that all these occurred during the tenure of the previous Congress-led UPA regime. Singh also mentioned paper leaks under various state governments led by the Opposition parties in states like UP, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal.

Singh gave details of enhancement of punishments for exam irregularities under the new Bill, of how fast-track courts have been set up, and how the deadlines of two months for investigations and three months for court rulings have been laid down in it.

“We are debating a Bill that is an amended version of a 2024 law – but no action has been taken under that law against anyone,” Priyanka said. “Using face recognition, the identities of the protesting students are being disclosed, but the same was not done for those involved in paper leaks.”

“Apni saakh bachaiye, apni neeyat theek kariye, apni akad ka ilaaj keejiye (save your reputation, correct your intentions, treat your arrogance),” she said.

Priyanka alleged that there had been “chori (theft)” in votes as well as at the Ram temple in Ayodhya, but “the biggest theft was the one of the future and dreams of the youths”. “If the youths become hopeless, it will be the country’s defeat, and we in the Opposition will die but not let the country lose,” she said.

Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Akhilesh Yadav said the police “oppression” perpetrated against the students during their protests was no less than what happened during the Emergency. He said that batons were used even then, but this time “electric current” was allegedly applied on students too.

He said this when Union minister Kiren Rijiju sought to know whether he would support a government that brought a Bill to respond to students or those who imposed the Emergency.

Akhilesh said that just like there was a regime change after the Emergency, there would be a regime change this time too. He said that even God would not save the government since its members were involved in the maha paap (grave sin) of chadhaava chori (theft of temple donations).

He accused the government of allegedly shutting down more than one lakh primary schools so that children of the poor and Dalits would not get a chance to study, adding that people of a particular shade (ekrangee) had been placed in top positions in higher educational institutions.

Earlier, initiating the discussion on the Bill, Gogoi, the Congress’s deputy leader in the House, said that after the 2024 NEET leak, 44 of the 45 accused chargesheeted had got bail, while its main accused Sanjeev Mukhia had remained absconding for 11 months before being arrested.

“We want to know who are the 47 people terminated by NTA (National Testing Agency), as the sanctioned capacity of NTA is 34. Are these outsourced people who you had brought there?” he asked, wondering why the DG, NTA, was removed but the chairman has been retained. “He (NTA chairman) is related to a specific organisation,” Gogoi said, alleging that there was corruption under him when he was heading the Public Service Commission of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. He charged that since the education department was important for the RSS, the government did not want education reforms. He claimed that education was being used for ideological indoctrination.

On behalf of the ruling NDA, young MPs such as Tejasvi Surya (BJP), Bansuri Swaraj (BJP), and Shrikant Shinde (Shiv Sena) were among those who spoke on the Bill.

Surya said the Modi government’s model was one of turning crises into opportunities, and that the government was responding to the recent NEET crisis in a manner that would fundamentally reform the education and exam system.

Bansuri praised the Bill for speeding up investigations and setting up fast-track courts, saying this marked an important step towards a solution.

Shrikant suggested that instead of having just one annual competition exam for which students invest years, there should be multiple exams even if the admission takes place once a year. He explained that this would protect students from losing one year in the event of any eventuality.

NCP(SP) leader Supriya Sule urged the House to think of parents whose children were facing exam leaks. Among other Opposition leaders who participated in the debate were Congress MP K C Venugopal and Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Abhishek Banerjee.

The amended Bill provides for a jail term up to 10 years, up from three to five years in the 2024 Act, and penalty up to Rs 50 lakh instead of the earlier Rs 10 lakh. If the crime is found to be organised, the Bill proposes a minimum sentence of seven years and a penalty of up to Rs 10 crore.

It also sets a two-month deadline to complete investigations into paper leak cases. According to the Bill, states and Union Territories will be empowered to set up fast-track courts that can complete the trial within three months of filing of the chargesheet. The Centre, it says, will be empowered to set up a special task force to probe some paper leak cases.

On Sunday, PM Modi also announced a high-powered task force on exam reforms led by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani.

World.title: 2,000 farmers march towards Bhopal, bedding and cooking material in hand
World.content:
Carrying sacks of grain, rolled-up bedding, cooking utensils and enough food to last a week, nearly 2,000 farmers marched into the outskirts of Bhopal on Tuesday after breaking through police barricades at the city’s southern edge, escalating a crop procurement dispute into one of the biggest political confrontations faced by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav’s government this year.

The farmers, representing 19 organisations under the banner of the Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM), have announced that they will not leave until the government agrees to procure 100% of the state’s moong crop and addresses long-standing grievances over fertiliser distribution.

On Tuesday night, the procession reached districts located near the outskirts of Bhopal, where scores of policemen were deployed and attempted to stop them with multiple layers of barricades.

The farmers’ march to Bhopal was triggered primarily by demands for assured procurement of moong at the Minimum Support Price (MSP). Farmers’ groups say that while the Centre has announced 100% MSP procurement for tur, urad and masur, moong procurement continues to be governed by the Price Support Scheme, under which procurement is generally capped at 25% of a state’s estimated production. They argue that the ceiling leaves a large share of the harvest to be sold in the open market, where prices are significantly below the MSP of Rs 8,768 per quintal for the 2026–27 season.

A farmer leader, Santosh Patwari, said, “We have been mobilising for over 20 days now. We had no option but to protest after we did not hear from the government despite sending multiple representations to the government. The farmers are unable to get a profitable rate for the sale of their moong produce, and we have no option but to go to the CM’s residence.”



The mobilisation began in Narmadapuram, where farmers first assembled at Sethani Ghat before beginning their march towards Bhopal. The administration initially prevented the procession from moving, triggering a sit-in protest. As evening approached and tensions mounted, authorities removed the barricades, allowing the march to continue. On Tuesday, the convoy advanced through Obaidullaganj and Raisen district towards the capital. Police again erected barricades at several locations, including toll plazas and the Mandideep border, while officials urged farmer leaders to hand over a memorandum instead of proceeding into Bhopal.

Wider discontent

The protest also reflects wider discontent in rural Madhya Pradesh. Farmers’ organisations say procurement delays, quantity caps, registration problems and recurring fertiliser shortages have become common over successive crop seasons. With cultivation costs rising and market prices remaining uncertain, they argue that many growers are being forced into distress sales despite good production.



The agitation presents another political challenge for the Mohan Yadav government, which only months ago was forced to dilute its proposed land-pooling policy for the 2028 Simhastha after sustained protests by farmers in Ujjain. Following weeks of demonstrations, the government revised several provisions of the policy and assured farmers that land would not be acquired without their consent.

Farmers’ organisations have also accused the administration of trying to prevent supporters from reaching Bhopal by placing barricades on roads leading out of villages in districts including Raisen, Vidisha, Harda, Narmadapuram and Budhni.

The administration has denied any attempt to suppress the protest, saying police deployment was aimed at maintaining law and order. Additional SP (Hoshangabad) Anil Sharma said, “The last point of the protest will be maintained at Hoshangabad, and we are constantly talking to the farmers to address their demands in a peaceful manner. There are all facilities here, and we have proper force to manage the situation.”

World.title: ‘Granted leave only after stillbirth’, teacher’s family claims officials demanded Rs 50,000 bribe
World.content:
The stillbirth of a government school teacher’s baby after a prolonged delay in the processing of her leave application has triggered allegations of bribery against officials of the education department in Jharkhand’s Palamu. While the district administration ordered an inquiry, it rejected the family’s allegations of corruption.

Bharti Pandey, a teacher at Plus Two High School, Tarhasi, who was on deputation at Kasturba Gandhi CM Excellence School, Chainpur, had applied for child care leave (CCL) on July 3.

Her husband, Mukesh Kumar Tiwari, a police officer posted in Hazaribagh, alleged that staff from the district education department demanded a bribe of nearly Rs 50,000 to process the application, forcing his wife to continue travelling in the final weeks of her pregnancy.

On July 25, she was admitted to Sona Nursing Home in Medininagar, where doctors declared that the foetus had died in the womb.

Tiwari told The Indian Express, “We applied for child care leave because my wife already has two children and maternity leave was not applicable. But instead of processing the application, they kept asking for money and making us run from one office to another.”

He alleged that the officials initially demanded Rs 30,000, but later they said “more than Rs 50,000 would be required”.

Tiwari claimed that he, along with office-bearers of the Jharkhand Madhyamik Shikshak Sangh, met Deputy Commissioner Dilip Pratap Singh Shekhawat a week earlier and informed him that officials were demanding money to sanction the leave. “The DC sir called the DEO (District Education Officer) in front of us and directed him to resolve the issue immediately. But when I again met the DEO, he told me, ‘Go and get your leave from the DC’,” Tiwari alleged.

Severe abdominal pain



Tiwari further said his wife continued reporting for duty despite being in the last stage of pregnancy. On July 25, after another visit to the DEO office, she developed severe abdominal pain and was rushed to the hospital.
